item.title: Uniform duplication-divergence random graphs I: Degrees and Local Limits
item.description: arXiv:2611.00123v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a growing random graph in which each new vertex chooses a uniformly random parent, joins that parent with probability $r\in(0,1]$, and independently joins each of the parent's current neighbors with probability $p\in(0,1)$. Let $p_c$ be the unique solution of $p_c e^{p_c}=1$. For $0<p<p_c$, we prove that the empirical degree distribution converges in probability to the stationary distribution $\pi$ of an explicit reset-and-growth Markov chain. Its upper tail satisfies $\pi((y,\infty))\sim C_{p,r}y^{-\kappa}$, where $C_{p,r}>0$ and $\kappa>0$ solves $p^\kappa+p\kappa=1$. This confirms predictions from physics (Lambiotte, Krapivsky, Bhat and Redner, \textit{Physical Review Letters}, 2016). We further show that for every fixed radius $\ell$ and $p<p_c$, the empirical distribution of induced rooted $\ell$-neighborhoods converges to the invariant law of a graph-valued reset-and-growth Markov process. We give an explicit construction of the limiting graph using a marked ancestral genealogy. Its root component is almost surely finite for $r<1$, and infinite with exactly one end for $r=1$. Moreover, for every $0<p<1$, both the fixed-vertex degrees and the maximum degree grow on the scale $t^p$, and the vertex of maximum degree is eventually unique and persistent.
item.dc:creator: Partha S. Dey, Neeladri Maitra, Jaya M. Manthripragada, Grigory Terlov

item.title: Two moments suffice for Bessel approximation: conditioned differences, contingency tables, and probabilistic divide-and-conquer
item.description: arXiv:2611.00263v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop Stein's method, with explicit constants throughout, for the discrete Bessel distribution: the law of a Poisson variable given its difference from an independent Poisson variable. The Bessel family is characterized by a birth-death operator with quadratic death rate $n(n+k)$ and as the exact fixed-point set of a centered quadratic-bias transform, and we prove a dependency expansion of Arratia-Goldstein-Gordon type: two joint moments of a column array control the total-variation distance from the conditioned row sum to a matched Bessel law. Applied to the row-constrained Fisher-Yates ensemble on $2\times c$ contingency tables -- independent Bernoulli or capped-Poisson entries conditioned on the row-sum difference, column sums free -- this yields a limit theorem -- which upgrades to the entire conditioned table at the same two-moment error -- a completely explicit enumeration estimate, and an exact divide-and-conquer sampler with certified acceptance. The entire apparatus -- operator, expansion, enumeration, sampler -- generalizes to $r\times c$ tables, where conditioning on all successive row differences produces a hyper-Bessel law. Verification scripts are included as ancillary files.
item.dc:creator: Stephen DeSalvo

item.title: Stein's method for negative binomial and hyper-negative-binomial laws, with applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.00275v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop Stein's method for the negative binomial law and for the hyper-negative-binomial law, the law of the smallest row total of an array of independent geometric variables given the differences of the row totals, with every constant explicit. The main instrument is a comparison of two biasings of the approximated variable, which cancels the rate term exactly at the matched parameter. We provide total variation bounds for sums of independent geometric variables at drifting parameters, for sums of dependent geometric variables (the Arratia-Goldstein-Gordon theorem with geometric summands and the Poisson law as an endpoint), and for Poisson mixtures; the exact conditional law of negative-binomial counts given their differences, with the Bessel law as its Poisson limit; and a dependency expansion for the column direction of a contingency table. A final section verifies every bound numerically, with one script per result.
item.dc:creator: Stephen DeSalvo

item.title: Exact Asymptotics for the Harmonic Descent Chain and Extended Convergence Bounds for Recursive Statistics
item.description: arXiv:2611.00347v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give an exact asymptotic expansion of the occupation probabilities $a(n,k)$ of the harmonic descent chain, introduced by D. Aldous, as $n\rightarrow\infty$ with $k\in\mathrm{o}(\sqrt{n})$. In addition, we extend the recent results of Brandenberger et al. by giving a bound on the rate of convergence of sequences defined recursively by $x_n = \frac{1}{H_{n-1}}\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}\frac{x_i}{n-i}$ for more general initial conditions. This result enables the application of an existing central limit theorem, also by Brandenberger et al., to statistics of the critical beta-splitting tree which satisfy our more general initial conditions.
item.dc:creator: Sean P. Svihla

item.title: Stability, discretization, and optimality of continuous-time causal optimal transport
item.description: arXiv:2611.00353v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove stability of continuous-time causal and bicausal optimal transport problems when both marginals converge in adapted Wasserstein distance along common vanishing time shifts. The marginal laws, filtrations, and costs may all vary, while the limit remains the original causal or bicausal transport problem. This allows for time discretization and the approximation of transport problems between non-degenerate scalar fractional stochastic differential equations by their Wong--Zakai schemes. We further establish sufficient conditions so that the synchronous coupling is optimal for the bicausal transport problem between scalar fractional stochastic differential equations under continuous, nonnegative submodular costs of polynomial growth. This result covers all Hurst parameters \(H\in(0,1)\) up to an additional order-preserving commutator condition on the corresponding coefficients for the rough regime \(H\in(0,1/2)\).
item.dc:creator: Yifan Jiang, Fang Rui Lim

item.title: Absorption Probabilities for Brownian Convex Hulls in Arbitrary Dimension
item.description: arXiv:2611.00381v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every dimension $d\ge1$, we determine the probability that a prescribed point in $\mathbb R^d$ belongs to the convex hull over $[0,1]$ of a standard Brownian motion starting at the origin or of a Brownian bridge from $0$ to $0$. We obtain explicit one-dimensional integral formulas involving only standard special functions. For example, in dimension three the Brownian-motion absorption probability $p_3^B(r)$ for a prescribed point at distance $r>0$ from the origin is \[ p_3^B(r) =\frac{r}{\sqrt2\,\pi^{3/2}} \int_0^\infty \left(\frac{\pi}{2\sqrt{1+v^2}}-1\right) \mathrm{e}^{-r^2(1+v^2)/4} (K_1-K_0)\!\left(\frac{r^2(1+v^2)}4\right)\,\mathrm{d} v, \] where $K_\nu$ denotes the modified Bessel function of the second kind. For each fixed dimension $d\ge1$ and each prescribed nonzero point in $\mathbb R^d$, we derive precise asymptotics of the non-absorption probabilities for the convex hulls of Brownian motion on $[0,T]$ and a Brownian bridge from $0$ to $0$ over the same interval, as $T\to\infty$. The corresponding probabilities are asymptotic to explicit positive constants times $T^{-1/2}(\log T)^{d-1}$ and $T^{-1}(\log T)^{d-1}$, respectively. We also consider the first time $\tau_d$ at which the growing convex hull of a standard Brownian motion in $\mathbb R^d$ absorbs a prescribed point at distance one from the origin. We determine the Mellin and Laplace transforms of $\tau_d$ explicitly. Although $\mathbb E[\tau_d]=\infty$ in every dimension, we prove \[ \frac{\log\tau_d-2d}{2\sqrt d} \xrightarrow{\mathrm d}N(0,1), \qquad d\to\infty. \] In particular, $\tau_d^{1/d}\to\mathrm{e}^2$ in probability, as $d\to\infty$. Surprisingly, the same limit holds for $S_d^{1/d}$, where $S_d$ is the first time at which the Brownian convex hull contains the entire unit ball.
item.dc:creator: Zakhar Kabluchko

item.title: Universality of Large-Scale Geometry For Critical Random-Cluster Models
item.description: arXiv:2611.00425v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The understanding of the behaviour of critical lattice models in two dimensions has made immense progress in the past couple of decades, with conformal invariance as its conjectured end goal. We consider here the critical random-cluster model (or FK-percolation) on a large class of graphs --- namely bi-periodic isoradial graphs --- with cluster-weight~$q \in [1,4]$. Following up on the establishment of rotational invariance at criticality in \cite{Rotation}, we prove that the large scale behaviour of these models is asymptotically the same on all such graphs. These include the critical homogeneous models on the square, triangular and hexagonal lattices.
item.dc:creator: Ulrik Thinggaard Hansen, Ioan Manolescu

item.title: On the asymptotic distribution of the largest eigenvalue of unbalanced complex Jacobi ensembles
item.description: arXiv:2611.00577v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathbf{A} \sim \mathbb{C}\mathcal{W}_p(I,m)$ and $\mathbf{B} \sim \mathbb{C}\mathcal{W}_p(I,n)$ be two independent complex Wishart random matrices. In this work, we investigate the asymptotic distribution of the largest eigenvalue $\theta_{\max}$ of the random matrix $\mathbf{J} = (\mathbf{A}+\mathbf{B})^{-1}\mathbf{B}$. The high-dimensional regime is potentially unbalanced in the sense that, as $p \to \infty$, $m$ may grow faster than $p$, whereas $n$ grows proportionally to $p$. The asymptotic behavior of $\theta_{\max}$ is characterized by means of a Riemann-Hilbert (RH) problem for Jacobi polynomials with modified Jacobi weights. We establish the type 2 Tracy--Widom asymptotic distribution of $\theta_{\max}$. This provides an alternative, RH-based proof of the corresponding result of Johnstone [Ann. Statist. 36 (2008), 2638-2716] in the balanced regime, and establishes a conjecture of Jiang [Probab. Theory Relat. Fields 144 (2009), 221-246] in the unbalanced regime. In addition, we obtain an explicit correction of order $p^{-2/3}$ to the Tracy--Widom approximation, with a remainder of order $\mathcal{O}(p^{-1})$, and show exponential decay, as a function of $p$, of the upper tail of the distribution of $\theta_{\max}$.
item.dc:creator: Gustavo Didier, Aikaterini Gkogkou, John Lopez Santander, Kenneth D. T-R McLaughlin

item.title: Quantum Diffusion and the Block-Size Crossover in the Block Anderson Model
item.description: arXiv:2611.00598v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the block Anderson Hamiltonian \(H_L=\lambda\Psi_L+\mathcal V\) on the discrete torus \((\mathbb Z/L\mathbb Z)^d\), \(d\geq2\), where \(\Psi_L\) is the nearest-neighbor Laplacian and \(\mathcal V\) consists of independent \(W^d\times W^d\) GOE blocks. In the weak-disorder limit \(\lambda\to\infty\), we establish an entrywise local law, a spatial scaling limit for the squared resolvent entries, time-averaged dynamical delocalization, and lower bounds on the localization length of most bulk eigenfunctions. Particularly, we allow the block size to be fixed or grow above a polylogarithmic threshold. In sufficiently large polynomial volumes, the dynamical estimates hold for \(C_\delta(\lambda+W/\lambda)\leq T\leq \lambda^{1+\kappa_d^{\rm BA}-\delta}\), with a dimension-dependent exponent \(\kappa_d^{\rm BA}>0\), and the spreading scale is \(\sqrt{(\lambda^3+\lambda W)T}\). This identifies a transition at \(W\asymp\lambda^2\) between \(\lambda^{3/2}\sqrt T\) and \(\sqrt{\lambda WT}\). The proof combines Gaussian moment estimates with deterministic stability of a matrix Dyson equation. A partial Bloch transform handles fixed blocks, while scalar reduction controls growing blocks. A Feshbach--Schur reduction of the block \(T\)-equation separates a single scalar diffusion mode from the stable internal cell modes. A renewal expansion and exact cell counting give a positive representation of the diffusion coefficient and control the fourth moment uniformly across the block-size transition. Notably, our argument does not require an enumeration of Feynman diagrams.
item.dc:creator: Haoxuan Fu

item.title: CLT for the Weight of the Minimum Spanning Arborescence on the Complete Directed Graph
item.description: arXiv:2611.00698v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The minimum spanning arborescence (MSA) with a fixed boundary, defined on weighted directed graphs, is the directed analogue of the minimum spanning tree (MST). The behaviour of the MSA has been of recent interest and is known to be quite different from that of its undirected counterpart. On the complete directed graph, and for edge weights given by i.i.d. random variables with a broad class of distributions, we prove a Central Limit Theorem for the weight of the MSA with appropriate scaling. While the scaling for the CLT is similar to MST case explored by Janson, the centering required ($1$ as opposed to $\zeta(3)$ for Uniform$[0,1]$ weights) and the limiting variance of the Gaussian ($1$ as opposed to $6\zeta(4)-4\zeta(3)$ for Uniform$[0,1]$ weights) are notably different.
item.dc:creator: Swarnadeep Bagchi, Pablo de la Fuente, Kesav Krishnan

item.title: Free energy of spherical vector spin glasses
item.description: arXiv:2611.00710v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We identify the limit free energy of spherical vector spin glasses by a variational formula. The covariance function need not be convex. Using the global symmetry of the spin configurations, we introduce a family of constraint measures that gives a disintegration of the original spin distribution. We first identify the limit free energy of each constrained model and then apply the Laplace method to recover that of the original model.
item.dc:creator: Hong-Bin Chen

item.title: Cutoff for Simple Random Walk on Preferential Attachment Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.00717v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider simple random walk on the sequential affine preferential attachment graphs with fixed parameters $m\ge2$ and $\delta\ge0$. We prove the walk has total-variation cutoff, and for every fixed $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, \[ t_{\mathrm{mix}}^{(n)}(\varepsilon) =\frac{\log n}{\nu d} +O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(\sqrt{\log n}\right), \] where $\nu>0$ is the walk speed and $d>0$ is the entropy per level of harmonic measure on the P\'olya--point tree, the local weak limit of the graph. Thus cutoff occurs at the entropic time. Entropic cutoff was previously established for a range of random graph models including configuration models under mild degree assumptions and on Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi random graphs for typical starting points. We extend the harmonic-measure approach to preferential attachment, accounting for its age-dependent structure and hubs of polynomial degree. The local weak limit, the P\'olya--point tree, provides a more tractable setting for analyzing the walk. The proof combines regeneration estimates on the local limit tree, a quantitative graph--tree coupling on the mixing-time scale, and control of hub excursions. We show that shortly before the cutoff time its distribution is close in total variation distance to a measure with small $L^\infty$ distance from stationarity. When $m\ge2$, the spectral gap is bounded away from zero with high probability which completes the upper-bound coupling argument.
item.dc:creator: Allan Sly, Seoyeon Yang

item.title: Free energy of 2-spin spherical vector spin glasses
item.description: arXiv:2611.00747v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compute the limit of free energy of 2-spin spherical vector spin glasses with possibly non-convex interaction and couplings satisfying a finite fourth-moment assumption. The couplings need not be Gaussian. The limit is given by a logarithmic-determinant variational formula, equivalently by a finite-dimensional matrix Dyson equation, and its zero-temperature limit yields the ground-state energy. The limiting formulas depend only on the covariance of the couplings. We also study fluctuations: at an interior minimizer, an explicit variance bound transfers the limiting law of a logarithmic linear statistic to the free energy. For Gaussian couplings, this yields Gaussian fluctuations. At a boundary minimizer, assuming a simple regular edge with GOE Tracy-Widom fluctuations and a one-edge reduction, we transfer the edge fluctuations to the free energy.
item.dc:creator: Hong-Bin Chen, Yanjin Xiang, Zhihua Zhang

item.title: The Self-repelling Burglar
item.description: arXiv:2611.00854v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the conditional location of $X_T$ given the local time profile $L_T(\cdot)$ for two non-Markovian self-interacting processes: the polynomially self-repelling motion (PSRM) and the true self-repelling motion (TSRM). For TSRM, our novel approach yields a new proof of Dumaz's clever burglar result [Dumaz 2012].
item.dc:creator: Yaolin Yu

item.title: A dual approach to $L^p$ estimates for orthogonal martingales satisfying the differential subordination
item.description: arXiv:2611.00932v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a new dual approach, which can be used to establish sharp $L^p$ bounds for orthogonal differentially subordinate martingales. The method rests on the construction of a certain special function enjoying appropriate majorization properties and a novel differential condition.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Ba\~nuelos, Adam Os\k{e}kowski

item.title: Convergence of non-symmetric forms with changing reference measures
item.description: arXiv:2611.00975v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a functional-analytic theory of convergence for non-symmetric generalized Dirichlet forms defined on a sequence of Hilbert spaces $H_n$ converging to a limit space $H$ in the sense of Kuwae-Shioya, with the principal applications concerning $L^2$-spaces over varying reference measures $\mu_n \to \mu$. Extending Mosco's variational convergence for Dirichlet forms to the non-symmetric setting via a functional controlling the off diagonal values of the forms, we introduce a notion of generalized convergence of non-symmetric Dirichlet forms and show it to be equivalent to strong convergence of the associated resolvents, to weak convergence of the co-resolvents, and to strong graph convergence of the infinitesimal generators. A version of the Trotter-Kato theorem in the Kuwae-Shioya framework yields the corresponding equivalence for $C_0$-contraction semigroups. As applications, we give sufficient conditions for the generalized convergence of elliptic and sectorial $a_{i,j}$-forms with changing speed measures, both on $\mathbb{R}^d$ and in infinite dimensions over a Gelfand triple, and deduce weak convergence of the laws of the associated right processes under tightness of the path measures.
item.dc:creator: Jonas M. T\"olle

item.title: Invariant universal averages and Bertrand's paradox: a response to Shackel
item.description: arXiv:2611.00981v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 2014, with D. Aerts we proposed a solution to the hard problem of Bertrand's paradox by means of a universal average over different ways of randomizing an entity. In his recent monograph, N. Shackel raises objections concerning the approximation by cellular densities, the restrictions used in their construction, the apparently trivial limit of their averages, the choice of a second-order probability law, and the dependence of the result on the naming of chords. We revisit these objections using the invariance-based formulation of the universal average. The first objection is well taken, and the approximation argument is repaired: an explicit sequence of bivalent cellular densities provides weak approximation of any prescribed probability measure, with an error bound for intervals. We show that any second-order selection law invariant under rearrangements of equal-length cells has the same uniform barycenter, independently of the particular densities and weights employed. For cellular densities, this conclusion holds exactly at every finite resolution. Thus, non-uniqueness of the second-order law does not prevent uniqueness of the resulting average within the indifferent class. Finally, we prove that no probability measure can be invariant under both these rearrangements and arbitrary changes of interval lengths. The reference geometry therefore cannot be obtained by averaging alone: it must be supplied by the physical modelization of the randomized entity. These results clarify the scope, and the limitations, of our original distinction between the easy and hard problems of Bertrand's paradox.
item.dc:creator: Massimiliano Sassoli de Bianchi

item.title: Two types of averaging principles for multiplicative stochastic Korteweg-de Vries equations with fast oscillations
item.description: arXiv:2611.01051v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study averaging principles for stochastic KdV equations perturbed by a fast oscillating term generated by a stochastic reaction-diffusion equation in $H^s(\mathbb{R})$, $ s\geq 0$. When dealing with multilinear estimates of the nonlinear terms in the stochastic KdV type equation, two kinds of workspace are both effective. The classical workspace can help us prove the averaging principle in the $L_\omega^2$ sense, but it has more restrictions on the noise kernel and the conservation structures. When we use a new workspace without homogeneous low frequency restrictions, only the regularity conditions and the $L_x^2$ conservation structure is needed. Correspondingly, because there is no moment estimate of the solution, we can only prove the perturbed equations converge to an averaging equation in the probability sense. Our works may have important reference value, because it not only provides a new perspective to handle dynamical problems of stochastic dispersive model, but also compare it with the classical method.
item.dc:creator: Jie Chen, Fan Gu, Xianliang Zhao

item.title: A characterization and closure property of Thorin's class
item.description: arXiv:2611.01058v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Thorin's class coincides with the smallest class of probability laws on $\mathbb{R}$ that contains all gamma laws and their reflections, while being closed under convolution and weak convergence. In particular, all Thorin laws are self-decomposable. This paper proves an alternative characterization of Thorin's class in terms of what we call the hyperbolic Bochner-Bernstein property. This property corresponds to the notion of hyperbolically completely monotone Laplace transforms on the positive half line, but extended to the real-valued setting. Using the new characterization, it is shown that Thorin's class is closed under multiplication with independent random variables admitting hyperbolically completely monotone densities, which partly settles an open question raised by Bondesson and allows for proving that a large class of possibly skewed real-valued distributions is in Thorin's class. As particular examples, we apply the closure property to show that Johnson's S\textsubscript{U} distribution and the Pearson type IV distribution are in Thorin's class for all parameter choices.
item.dc:creator: Thomas K. Kloster

item.title: From Gaussian to stable and back: Non-Pareto points in growing dimension
item.description: arXiv:2611.01096v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the number of non-Pareto points in two high-dimensional models: a homogeneous Poisson point process and a fixed-size sample of independent uniform points in the unit cube. A point is non-Pareto if some other sample point is coordinatewise less than or equal to it. As the dimension grows on the logarithmic scale of the intensity or sample size, the asymptotic behavior exhibits a surprising sequence of transitions: from Gaussian to stable fluctuations, back to Gaussian, then to a Poisson limit at the sparsity threshold, followed by the eventual disappearance of non-Pareto points. We identify the critical thresholds, normalizations, and limiting laws in both models. Notably, the return to Gaussianity occurs while the stability index remains strictly below $2$ and is driven by a change in the dominant fluctuation mechanism. Moreover, in part of the returning Gaussian regime, the natural normalization is the square root of the expected count rather than its standard deviation. At the stable--Gaussian transition, the two mechanisms can coexist, giving rise to a sum of independent stable and Gaussian random variables.
item.dc:creator: Chinmoy Bhattacharjee, Andrii Ilienko, Bochen Jin, Ilya Molchanov

item.title: Lyapunov functions for the Langevin equation with dissipative damping
item.description: arXiv:2611.01187v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the well-posedness and the large time stability of the Langevin equation in the presence of potentials and dissipative damping together with additive white noise. While the confining potential is assumed to be smooth, the nonlinear damping is allowed to have either polynomial growth or singular behaviors. We construct novel Lyapunov functions and determine the corresponding parameter regimes that lead to global well-posedness or finite-time explosion. These Lyapunov functions also allow for deriving quantitative mixing rates toward equilibrium. Our results extend existing ergodic theory established for the instance of nonlinear damping satisfying suitable integrability conditions.
item.dc:creator: Barkat Mian, Hung D. Nguyen

item.title: The Prodigal Elephant Returns: Last-Return Laws in the Superdiffusive Regime
item.description: arXiv:2611.01279v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $(S_n)$ be the one-dimensional elephant random walk with memory parameter $p\in(3/4,1)$ and first-step probability $q=\mathbb{P}(S_1=1)\in[0,1]$. Set $a=2p-1$, and let $f_{q,a}$ denote the density of the almost-sure limit of $S_n/n^a$. We prove that the last return time $T_0=\sup\{m\geq0:S_m=0\}$ satisfies: $\mathbb{P}(T_0\geq n)\sim f_{q,a}(0)\sqrt{\frac{8}{\pi(2a-1)}}n^{-(a-1/2)}$. Reflection gives $f_{q,a}(0)=f_{1,a}(0)$, so the constant is independent of $q$. For future walks started from admissible states $(n,x_n)$ with $x_n/\sqrt n\to z$, we establish functional convergence of the centered martingale-normalized paths to a time-changed Brownian motion. Uniform control of late hitting times then gives the eventual-return kernel $2\Phi(-\sqrt{2a-1}|z|)$, uniformly on bounded scaled windows, where $\Phi$ is the standard normal distribution function. The same last-visit asymptotic holds uniformly for nonempty deterministic targets $F_n\subseteq[-r_n,r_n]\cap\mathbb{Z}$, $r_n=o(\sqrt n)$, held fixed during each trajectory. Conditionally on $T_0\geq n$, we identify the joint limit of $S_n/\sqrt n$, the next return divided by $n$, and the last return divided by the next return. The last ratio converges to $A^{-1/(2a-1)}$, independently of the other two limiting coordinates, where $A$ has the arcsine distribution on $(0,1)$.
item.dc:creator: H\'elio Trinas

item.title: Stochastic Euler Products in the Paley-Wiener Space
item.description: arXiv:2611.01347v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: General sufficient conditions, in terms of stochastic Euler products, are given for a realization of a point process to have finite excess or finite deficiency in the Paley-Wiener space.
item.dc:creator: Alexander I. Bufetov

item.title: Decay of Correlations for Multiplicative Functionals of Determinantal Point Processes
item.description: arXiv:2611.01379v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The main result of this paper is an upper bound on the correlations of multiplicative functionals of determinantal point processes. In particular, for the sine process, the correlations of a multiplicative functional associated with a rapidly decaying function decay quadratically. It follows that the spectral density of such functionals belongs to the Sobolev space $H_1$.
item.dc:creator: Alexander I. Bufetov

item.title: Precise large deviations for the elephant random walk with Weibull-type and lognormal-type random step sizes
item.description: arXiv:2611.01440v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove precise large deviations for the symmetric elephant random walk with random step sizes. When the distribution of $|Z_1-1|$ is subexponential, we first show that, for each fixed$p\in[0,1]$, there exists a positive number sequence $b_n\to\infty$ such that \[ \mathbb P(S_n>x)\sim \mathbb P(S_n<-x)\sim \frac n2\overline F(x) \] uniformly for $x\ge b_n$, where $\overline F(x)=\mathbb P(|Z_1-1|>x)$. This existence result requires no moment assumptions and does not specify the growth rate of $b_n$. For $p\in[0,3/4]$, we further give explicit sufficient conditions on $b_n$ under Weibull-type and lognormal-type tail conditions with a regularly varying factor $x^\gamma L(x)$, where $\gamma\in\mathbf R$ and $L$ is a positive measurable slowly varying function. Analogous results hold with $\mathbb P(|Z_1|>x)$ and non-strict tails.
item.dc:creator: Shuyuan Liang

item.title: $p$-Wasserstein distance and Cram\'{e}r-type moderate deviations for the multi-dimensional elephant random walk
item.description: arXiv:2611.01443v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish $p$-Wasserstein bounds and Cram\'{e}r-type moderate deviations for the multi-dimensional elephant random walk in the diffusive and critical regimes. Using a Gaussian convolution estimate with random covariance and the recursions for the conditional covariance, we obtain $W_{p,2}(\mathcal L(\widehat T_n),N(0,I_d))\le C_{a,d}pL_n$, where $\widehat T_n$ is normalized by its exact covariance and \[ L_n\asymp \begin{cases} n^{-1/2}\log n,&a\le1/3,\\ n^{-3(1/2-a)},&1/3<a<1/2,\\ (\log n)^{-3/2},&a=1/2. \end{cases} \] Consequently, we obtain radial Cram\'{e}r-type moderate deviations for $x=o(L_n^{-1/3})$. We also determine the covariance bias under the uncorrected normalization and establish the corresponding Wasserstein bounds, lower bounds and moderate deviation estimates. The dimension and the model parameters are fixed.
item.dc:creator: Shuyuan Liang

item.title: Local Limit Theorem for Branching Processes in Varying Environments
item.description: arXiv:2611.01455v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $Z_{i,n}$ be the population at time $n$ descended from one particle at time $i$ in a branching process in a varying environment. Under two-sided bounds on products of offspring means, an integrable uniform second-moment tail condition, and nondegeneracy and unit positive-support gcd of all weak limits, we prove $\mathbb{P}(Z_{i,n}=k)\le C(n-i+1)^{-2}$ uniformly in $0\le i<n$ and $k\ge1$, and obtain a local limit theorem as $n-i,k\to\infty$ with $k\le L_0(n-i)$, without third-moment assumptions. These results extend the classical local probability estimates for critical Galton--Watson processes to varying environments.
item.dc:creator: Zhiyang Xia, Mei Zhang

item.title: Half-space polynuclear growth: KPZ universality
item.description: arXiv:2611.01475v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study polynuclear growth (PNG) on the half-line with Poisson nucleations in the bulk and at the boundary. For every nonnegative boundary nucleation rate, we construct stationary measures and jointly stationary couplings under a common graphical environment, with profiles pinned at the origin. We realize these couplings as a measurable stationary PNG horizon and prove convergence to the half-space stationary horizon under Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) scaling. The horizon convergence includes its base profile and positive representing measure, together with joint profile convergence at every prescribed finite parameter list. We also prove convergence of the height evolution from general upper-semicontinuous initial profiles to the half-space KPZ fixed point. The associated passage field converges locally uniformly to the half-space directed landscape, jointly with evolutions from finitely many initial profiles driven by the same environment. The convergence results cover the critical boundary window and every fixed subcritical boundary rate, including zero. All fixed subcritical rates produce the same limiting laws.
item.dc:creator: Kailun Chen

item.title: No infinite cluster at criticality for long-range percolation with fast-decaying interactions
item.description: arXiv:2611.01490v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider independent long-range bond percolation on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ in which $x$ and $y$ are joined with probability $1-e^{-\beta J(x-y)}$. Let $d\ge2$ and let $J$ be invariant under coordinate permutations and sign changes, positive on nearest-neighbour pairs, and satisfy $\liminf_{n\to\infty} n^d\sum_{\|x\|>n}J(x)=0$. We prove that there is no infinite cluster at the critical parameter. Together with Berger's theorem for heavy tails, this gives continuity of the phase transition for $J(x)\asymp\|x\|^{-d-\alpha}$ for every $\alpha>0$ except $\alpha=d$, in every dimension $d\ge2$, and for every exponentially decaying kernel satisfying these hypotheses. Previously the fast-decaying case was known for nearest-neighbour and uniform finite-range kernels, in $d=2$ for finite-range and exponential kernels, and in high dimension for sufficiently spread-out kernels. The proof adapts a recent renormalization argument for nearest-neighbour percolation on $\mathbb{Z}^3$ that is driven by a gluing inequality conjectured by Kozma and Nitzan. Long edges enter in two places: they can jump over the surfaces that a nearest-neighbour path must cross, and they let a cluster outside a box enter it from far away. We control the first with thick outer faces and the tail condition, and the second by measuring entrances through the total edge weight between a cluster and a box rather than through the number of boundary vertices.
item.dc:creator: Yan Ru Pei

item.title: Feynman--Kac Representation for Parabolic Equations with Memory: A New Class of BSDEs
item.description: arXiv:2611.01591v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper is concerned with the connection between parabolic equations with memory (MPEs, for short) and backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs, for short). To provide a probabilistic representation of MPEs, we introduce a new class of BSDEs, called BSDEs with memory (MBSDEs, for short). The main feature of MBSDEs is that, at the current time $s$, the generator depends not only on the current value $Y^{t,x}(s)\equiv Y^{s,X^{t,x}(s)}(s)$ but also on the future path $r\mapsto Y^{r,X^{t,x}(s)}(r)$, $r\in[s,T]$. This structure reveals a fundamental difference from classical BSDEs: in the classical setting, the time and space variables are coupled and inseparable, whereas in MBSDEs they are completely independent. We prove the well-posedness of these MBSDEs and show that their adapted solutions provide a probabilistic representation for the solutions of MPEs. Furthermore, under a monotonicity condition, we establish a comparison principle for one-dimensional MBSDEs, which enables us to develop a viscosity solution theory for MPEs. This generalizes the celebrated nonlinear Feynman--Kac formula of Peng [25] and Pardoux--Peng [22] to the case with memory, in both the classical and viscosity solution senses.
item.dc:creator: Hanxiao Wang, Jiongmin Yong, Qi Zhang

item.title: Cutoff and a Gaussian-shift profile for the Rudvalis shuffle
item.description: arXiv:2611.01597v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Rudvalis shuffle removes the top card and reinserts it uniformly at random in one of the bottom two positions. Hildebrand proved the classical upper bound $O(n^3\log n)$, and Wilson later proved the sharp lower coefficient $1/(8\pi^2)$, establishing the correct order but leaving the leading upper constant, cutoff, and the cutoff profile open. We prove that the full labelled shuffle has total-variation cutoff at \[ \frac{n^3\log n}{8\pi^2} \] with a window of order $n^3$. The upper bound is obtained by writing one deterministic rotation of the shuffle as a nonnormal sweep of adjacent averaging projections, comparing that sweep to a weighted interchange generator, and controlling the entire regular-representation heat trace. The key sharp-window ingredients are heat-kernel smoothing through the Octopus Inequality, zero extension of deletion-harmonic ordered-tuple functions, a representation-theoretic multiplicity payment, and a sectorwise entrance estimate that disposes of all large Young-diagram deficits. For the profile, an exact complex one-card eigenfunction yields a deck statistic whose surviving first Fourier mode converges to a Gaussian shift. A matching full-deck $L^2$ bound then shows that this one-dimensional Gaussian likelihood ratio asymptotically exhausts all remaining information, giving the exact total-variation profile.
item.dc:creator: Yunjiang Jiang

item.title: Stochastic Orders of the Exit Pair and the Monotone Response to Resetting
item.description: arXiv:2611.01756v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Resetting a process, that is, restarting it from its initial position at random times, changes the probability that it leaves an interval through one end rather than the other. We show that the direction of this change is governed by how the exit time depends on the exit side, and we express this through classical stochastic orders. For random walks and birth-death chains we determine when resetting more intensively always moves the exit probability in the same direction, and we show that this can fail: we give an explicit chain in which the direction reverses twice over time, and bound the number of such reversals spectrally. We also show how the direction depends on the starting point. In the continuum limit we obtain the corresponding results for diffusions with drift.
item.dc:creator: Tony Newton, Juan Antonio Vega Coso

item.title: Critical characteristic-polynomial chaos for complex iid matrices
item.description: arXiv:2611.01794v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove convergence to critical Gaussian multiplicative chaos for characteristic-polynomial measures of complex iid matrices. Let $A_N=N^{-1/2}(\xi_{ij})$, with a fixed law satisfying $\mathbb E\xi=\mathbb E\xi^2=0$, $\mathbb E|\xi|^2=1$, and finite moments of every order; no density is assumed. On each fixed disk $\{|z|\le r\}$, $0<r<1$, expectation-normalized determinant measures at power $2\sqrt2$, multiplied by $\sqrt{\tfrac12\log N}$, converge to critical chaos with a fourth-cumulant covariance correction. The normalized height-deficit marked measure converges to the product of this spatial limit and the standard Rayleigh law. Convergence holds jointly with centered averages of the $\sqrt2$-scaled original logarithmic field against finitely many smooth compactly supported bulk tests, and with the two-sided near-critical curve at powers $q=2\sqrt2-2\lambda/\sqrt{\log N}$. On fixed compact parameter intervals, the curve converges in law in the uniform weak topology; all limiting coordinates use the same Gaussian field. The limiting curve is an explicit deterministic profile times the same critical measure.
item.dc:creator: Yin Cai, Xiang Fang, Feng Guo

item.title: The Laplace transform of the time of ruin in the Cram\'er--Lundberg model with Erlang $E_2(\mu)$ claims: spectrum, exact moments and matrix reduction
item.description: arXiv:2611.01886v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Laplace transform of the time of ruin in the classical Cram\'er--Lundberg model with claims having an Erlang distribution of shape parameter 2. We derive an integro-differential equation with two boundary conditions. For every positive discount rate, we show that its characteristic polynomial has one negative root and two distinct positive roots. Boundedness excludes the growing exponential term and yields a representation of the transform as a sum of two decaying exponentials. We construct a finite-dimensional matrix reduction of the convolution chain. For a model parameter set, we obtain exact expressions for the ruin probability, the mean time of ruin, and higher moments, including the third moment at zero initial surplus. We prove analyticity in the discount rate and justify the resulting moment series. We consider the analytic continuation of the representation to negative discount rates separately. For Erlang claims with an arbitrary positive integer shape parameter, we establish a closed linear system and the asymptotics of the root continuing the zero root at zero discount.
item.dc:creator: Goluba Yurieva

item.title: Reduction of the integro-differential equation to an ordinary differential equation in ruin models with investment in a risky asset
item.description: arXiv:2611.01892v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study ruin models with the surplus invested in a risky asset and Erlang-distributed claims: non-life insurance, annuity payments and the mixed model. Assuming that the integro-differential equation for the survival probability has a classical twice continuously differentiable solution, we prove that this solution satisfies a linear ordinary differential equation. We construct explicit annihilating operators and write the coefficients of the reduced equation in closed form through binomial coefficients (for the mixed model with equal shape parameters). A converse criterion is obtained: a bounded solution of the reduced equation satisfies the integro-differential equation if and only if the residual vanishes at zero initial capital together with its derivatives of order below that of the annihilator. The exponent of the power branch at infinity is determined by the parameters of the risky asset alone and does not depend on the shape parameter. For the mixed model we classify the fundamental set of solutions: the exponentially growing modes are excluded by boundedness. The connection coefficient of the power branch is nonzero by a known power-law lower bound for the ruin probability, and in the annuity model by the reduced equation and the boundary condition at zero. Hence the ruin probability has power-law asymptotics with a positive constant for all shape parameters and all positive exponents, and a complete asymptotic expansion up to a multiplicative constant in all three models. For non-life insurance with Erlang claims of order two the expansion coefficients are computed by an explicit recurrence.
item.dc:creator: Goluba Yurieva

item.title: Well-posedness and Quantitative Stability for Degenerate Fokker--Planck Equations with Rough Coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2611.01894v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish quantitative stability and well-posedness for degenerate Fokker--Planck equations with Sobolev-regular and possibly fully degenerate diffusion coefficient. For two classes of rough drifts, stability estimates imply uniqueness, and existence is proved under suitable conditions. First, for anisotropic drifts with partial fractional Sobolev regularity, we prove both existence (as probability densities, essential for the probabilistic interpretation via superposition) and quantitative stability without imposing any growth conditions, covering the full range of fractional exponents and extending previous Lagrangian-flow results. Second, for drifts whose distributional gradients are given by singular integrals (e.g., Biot--Savart velocity fields from $L^1$ vorticity), we obtain stability estimates that allow the diffusion matrix to be time-space dependent and possibly degenerate, removing the prior restrictions of identity diffusion or bounded coefficients. Our results also recover the pure transport regime as a limiting case.
item.dc:creator: Huaiqian Li, Liying Mu

item.title: Convergence in law of the maximum of the Riemann zeta function on expanding intervals near the critical line
item.description: arXiv:2611.01905v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $T \to \infty$, let $\tau$ be uniformly distributed on $[T,2T]$, and let $\sigma = \sigma(T)$ be a deterministic real part approaching $1/2$ from the right. We establish the convergence in law of the recentered maximum of $\log|\zeta(\sigma + \mathrm{i}\tau + \mathrm{i} h)|$ over $I_{\theta} = \smash{[ - (\log T)^{\theta},(\log T)^{\theta}]}$, for every fixed $\theta > 0$. Under explicit conditions on the displacement $\sigma - 1/2$, the recentered maximum converges to a Gumbel distribution with scale parameter $1/(2\sqrt{1 + \theta})$. The recentering is an exact upper quantile of the one-point law of the associated Haar field $F_{h}^{\mathrm{H}} = \Re\sum_{p^{j}\leq X}U_{p}^{j}/(jp^{j(\sigma + \mathrm{i} h)})$, where the $U_{p}$ are independent and uniformly distributed on the complex unit circle. The positive constant in the limiting distribution is characterized by a Gaussian process describing the limiting microscopic increments of the Haar field around a high point. The result is established without the Riemann hypothesis.
item.dc:creator: Fr\'ed\'eric Ouimet

item.title: Generic point processes are intermittently hyperuniform and maximally rigid
item.description: arXiv:2611.01975v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the prevalence of hyperuniformity and spatial rigidity among translation- invariant ergodic simple point processes of fixed intensity, in a topology controlling local second moments. Hyperuniform processes are dense but meagre. We prove that intermittent hyperuniformity is residual: the number variance exhibits hyperuniform behavior along some sequences of radii and hyperfluctuating behavior along others. Maximal rigidity is also residual. Thus generic processes are maximally rigid but not hyperuniform. A local-to-global principle reduces the proofs to cross-section constructions for an arbitrary fixed essentially free ergodic $\mathbb{R}^d$-action. We also prove that processes admitting revival sequences form a residual set and exhibit near-quadratic variance along suitable van Hove sequences.
item.dc:creator: Michael Bj\"orklund

item.title: Volume Doubling and Geometric Inequalities on Graphs with Bakry-\'Emery Curvature
item.description: arXiv:2611.02010v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider irreducible reversible Markov chains whose nonzero off-diagonal transition probabilities are bounded below by $\epsilon>0$ and whose reversible measure satisfies $m_-\le m(x)\le\kappa m_-$. Under the Bakry--\'Emery curvature condition $\mathrm{CD}(K,\infty)$, with $K\in\mathbb{R}$, we establish Wang's log-Harnack inequality $$ P_t(\log f)(x)\le\log P_tf(y) +\frac{C\mathrm{dist}(x,y)^2}{\int_0^t e^{2Ks}\mathrm{d} s}, $$ for bounded positive $f$ bounded away from zero and all $x,y\in V$, where $C$ is a constant dependent only on $\varepsilon$. Building upon this inequality, we further prove volume doubling property: let $K_-:=\max\{-K,0\}$ $$ \mathrm{Vol}(B(o,2R))\le C_0\exp\!\bigl(C_1\sqrt{K_-}\,R\bigr) \mathrm{Vol}(B(o,R)),\qquad R>0, $$ where $C_0,C_1$ depend only on $\epsilon,\kappa$. If $d$ is the maximum combinatorial degree of the support graph, we further prove under $\mathrm{CD}(0,\infty)$ the sharp volume growth bound $\mathrm{Vol}(B(o,R))\le m_-CR^{\lfloor d/2\rfloor}$ for all $o$ and $R\geq 1$.
item.dc:creator: Yanlong Ding, Shiping Liu, Chiyu Zhou

item.title: Reverse Transportation and Harnack Inequalities for Underdamped Langevin in the Non-convex Setting
item.description: arXiv:2611.02020v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a dimension-free long-time reverse transportation, respectively Harnack inequality for the underdamped Langevin dynamics with non-convex potential. Specifically, we prove that for any two initial points $z,z'$ and $P_t$ the underdamped Langevin semigroup, it holds \begin{equation} \mathrm{KL}(\delta_z P_t|\delta_{z'}P_t) \leq C\mathrm{e}^{-\chi t}|z-z'|(\mathcal{R}\vee|z-z'|) \end{equation} for all $t>\delta$ where $\delta>0$ is arbitrarily small and $C=C(\delta),\mathcal{R},\chi>0$ are dimension free constants. In particular, our proof extends recent results which are restricted to either the convex underdamped or the non-convex but overdamped setting.
item.dc:creator: Andreas Habring, Laurenz Nagler

item.title: An entropic barrier to equilibration in the discrete nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation: Rigorous bounds for the microcanonical Brownian motion
item.description: arXiv:2611.02025v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The relaxation of the discrete nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation is known to slow down dramatically when the energy density $\varepsilon$ exceeds a critical value $\varepsilon_c$, where the system enters a condensed phase. Replacing the Hamiltonian dynamics by Brownian motion on the microcanonical surface of $N$ sites at fixed mass and energy, we prove rigorous upper and lower bounds on the equilibration time $\tau_{\mathrm{eq}}$, which is governed by the first non-zero eigenvalue $\lambda_1$ of the Laplacian on this surface. In the condensed phase the equilibration time is stretched exponential, not exponential, in the system size. The upper bounds on $\lambda_1$ come from trial functions: of one occupation for $\varepsilon<\varepsilon_c$, where the problem reduces to a Sturm-Liouville equation, and of two occupations for $\varepsilon>\varepsilon_c$, where they cross the bottleneck through which the condensate moves between sites. The lower bounds on $\lambda_1$ come from a Bochner-Reilly argument, with a vector field that compensates the concavity of the boundary. As a result, $\tau_{\mathrm{eq}}=O(1)$ for $\varepsilon<\varepsilon_c$, while for $\varepsilon>\varepsilon_c$, asymptotically in $N$, $(\sqrt{2}-1)\sqrt{\varepsilon-\varepsilon_c}\leq\ln\tau_{\mathrm{eq}}/\sqrt{N}\leq\sqrt{\varepsilon-\varepsilon_c}$. We conjecture that the left-hand bound is sharp and the right-hand one is not.
item.dc:creator: Claudio Arezzo, Antonello Scardicchio

item.title: Asymptotic behavior of some strongly critical decomposable multi-type Galton-Watson processes with immigration
item.description: arXiv:2611.02069v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior of a critical decomposable multi-type Galton-Watson process with immigration whose offspring mean matrix is triangular with diagonal entries 1. Under second-order moment conditions on the offspring and immigration distributions, we establish a functional limit theorem for the sequence of appropriately scaled processes, and describe the limit process as independent squared Bessel processes and some linear combinations of their iterated integral processes. Our work completes and extends some results of Foster and Ney (1978) for some strongly critical decomposable multi-type Galton-Watson processes with immigration.
item.dc:creator: Matyas Barczy, D\'aniel Bezd\'any

item.title: Adhesive riffle shuffles: one-parameter models and mixing bounds
item.description: arXiv:2611.02092v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compare four simple shuffles with one adhesion parameter $p$: a card-weighted sticky riffle, a block-weighted riffle, a midpoint-interpolation shuffle, and a correlated-label inverse riffle. Independent surviving contacts create contiguous blocks; no force or energy constants are fitted. We give polynomial upper bounds with explicit dependence on $p$, common adjacency-survival lower bounds, and a sharper information lower bound for interpolation. For fixed deck size $n\ge4$, the mixing time diverges as $\Theta((1-p)^{-1})$ for the three cut-first models, but as $\Theta((1-p)^{-2})$ for the correlated-label model. The latter distinction comes from whether one or two additional contact breaks are needed to escape cyclic rotations. For even $n$, unglued interpolation retains the lower bound $\Omega(\sqrt n\log n)$ and upper bound $O(n^{5/2}\log n)$. We distinguish proved bounds from conjectured scales, recover classical riffle cutoff under sufficiently small perturbations, and explain precisely where established results on clumpy shuffles apply. The fixed-parameter asymptotic orders of the new cut-first families and their possible cutoff remain unresolved.
item.dc:creator: Yunjiang Jiang

item.title: An $L\log L$ theory of sparse graph convergence
item.description: arXiv:2611.02187v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Borgs, Chayes, Cohn and Zhao developed a limit theory for sparse graphs based on $L^p$ upper regularity with $p>1$, where Holder's inequality controls small sets. We develop the analogous theory in the Orlicz class $L\log L$, replacing Holder by the Young-Fenchel inequality for $\Psi(u)=(1+u)\log(1+u)-u$ and $\Psi^*(v)=e^v-1-v$. We prove a weak regularity lemma for upper $\Psi$-regular graphons with $4^{O(1/\varepsilon^2)}$ parts, using the modular $\int\Psi$ as the energy; that upper $\Psi$-regular sequences have cut-metric convergent subsequences; that convergent sequences with $L\log L$ limits are upper $\Psi$-regular; and that $L\log L$ balls are cut-metric compact. The class strictly contains every $L^p$ class with $p>1$, and we give sparse $W$-random graphs that are upper $\Psi$-regular but not upper $L^p$ regular for any $p>1$. For graphs with a given degree sequence we prove, by Stein's method of exchangeable pairs with switchings, that if the average degree tends to infinity, the density to zero and the degree profile converges in $L^1$ to $\varphi$, uniformly random graphs converge in the normalized cut metric to $\varphi\otimes\varphi$, with no condition on the maximum degree; the sequence is upper $\Psi$-regular when $\varphi\in L\log L$. We also show that the maximum-entropy $\beta$-model is entrywise Chung-Lu when $d_{\max}^2=o(M)$, and that cut-closeness to it follows from a lower bound $e^{-o(M)}$ on its probability of having the prescribed degrees. Finally, $\Psi$ is the large deviation rate function of sparse Erdos-Renyi graphs up to a factor $1+O(1/\log\frac1p)$.
item.dc:creator: Behzad Mehrdad

item.title: The multivariate Berry-Esseen theorem with an absolute constant
item.description: arXiv:2611.02195v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the multivariate Berry--Esseen inequality for sums of independent random vectors holds with the same constant in every dimension. For independent centered random vectors $X_1,\ldots,X_n\in\mathbb{R}^d$ whose covariance matrices sum to $I_d$, we show that the distance between the distribution of their sum and $N(0,I_d)$, measured uniformly over convex sets, is at most $C_0\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbb{E}\|X_i\|_2^3$ for a universal constant $C_0$. The bound requires only finite third moments and holds uniformly in the dimension, the number of summands, and their distributions. It also yields the corresponding bound for independent and identically distributed vectors. In particular, $C_0$ can be chosen to be $980$.
item.dc:creator: Zhi Ling

item.title: Fisher--Hartwig asymptotics and critical moments for the circular beta ensemble
item.description: arXiv:2611.02205v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the joint moments of real powers of the absolute value of characteristic polynomials in the circular beta ensemble, for every $\beta>0$. At fixed distinct prescribed points, the Fisher--Hartwig formula holds for every exponent greater than $-1$, with explicit constants and a relative error bounded by a negative power of the matrix size $N$. For approaching points in the same integrable range, the error is bounded by a negative power of $N\delta_N$, provided that $N\delta_N\to\infty$ and the sum of the absolute values of the negative exponents is less than two. Here $\delta_N$ is the minimum distance between the prescribed points; this range includes every integrable pair of root exponents. For $q>0$ at the critical relation $pq^2=2\beta$, we prove the Keating--Wong asymptotic for the $p$th moment of the integral of the $q$th absolute power of the characteristic polynomial, for every real $p>1$. The leading asymptotic extends to every complex spatial weight in $L^p$. The proofs combine the recursion for orthogonal polynomials on the unit circle with conditional expectation identities for Gaussian multiplicative chaos and quantitative estimates for approaching singularities.
item.dc:creator: Reda Chhaibi, Pierre-Lo\"ic M\'eliot, Joseph Najnudel, Ashkan Nikeghbali

item.title: Random Walk on age-preferential random growth processes
item.description: arXiv:2611.02329v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies a class of \textbf{exponentially age-preferential random growth graphs} $G(m,\beta)$: at each time $n$ a new vertex $v_n$ is added, and $m$ edges are drawn to existing vertices independently, with the probability that a target $v_k$ is chosen proportional to $e^{\beta k}$ ($\beta>0$), so that the graph's growth strongly favors ``young'' vertices. We systematically investigate two fundamental probabilistic problems of this model and supply the proof details: (1)~\textbf{Recurrence}: when $\beta>0$, the simple random walk on $G$ is recurrent with probability $1$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:rec}); (2)~\textbf{Infinite collisions}: for every $\beta>0$, two independent simple random walks on $G$ meet infinitely often with probability $1$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:icp}). The core of the proof is the following: by the Borel--Cantelli lemma combined with the \textbf{memoryless property} of exponential weights, $G$ is almost surely ``sausage-like'' --- there exist infinitely many bottlenecks consisting of exactly $m$ parallel edges; the cascade of bottlenecks makes the effective resistance diverge, yielding recurrence; the renewal process $\{T_k\}$ constructed at the bottleneck times has i.i.d.\ stationary increments with finite moments of every order for the first-passage times, and combined with a moderate-deviation estimate we verify Peres' Green-function criterion for infinite collisions.
item.dc:creator: Jia-shan Tang, Feng Wang, Xian-Yuan Wu

item.title: The geometric case of the Erd\H{o}s Similarity Conjecture. A human exposition of the OpenAI proof
item.description: arXiv:2611.02454v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a fixed $q\in(0,1)$, can a set of positive Lebesgue measure avoid every translated and dilated copy of $\{q^n:n\ge1\}$? OpenAI's release of October 6, 2026 shows that it can, with a compact subset of $[0,1]$ whose measure is arbitrarily close to one. We give a detailed exposition of the proof, using only finite probability and basic measure theory. The proof removes a small open set intersecting every copy, obtained from a random construction: fair random choices, attached to the cells of nested grids, route each point down a finite tree, and at the leaf reached a further random choice removes the point with probability $p$. The removed set therefore has expected density $p$, however large the tree, while the branching gives each copy many independent chances to intersect it. Each chance depends on only part of the tree, so its outcome changes at only a controlled number of dilations, and a union bound over finitely many representative dilations then covers every dilation. We also relate the proof to the earlier random-cell arguments going back to Kolountzakis (Bull. London Math. Soc. 29 (1997), 415--424) and to recent work on two-fold sumsets (arXiv:2607.03584) and on Rajchman measures (arXiv:2609.04456), and we show how the method of conditional expectations makes the construction deterministic.
item.dc:creator: Alex Iosevich, Alexia Yavicoli

item.title: Uniform Dimension Theorem for SLE in Natural Time
item.description: arXiv:2611.02493v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $0<\kappa<8$, we prove a uniform dimension transformation theorem for SLE in natural time: on a single probability-one event, Hausdorff and packing dimensions of every time set are multiplied by $d=1+\kappa/8$, and the same holds for lower and upper box dimensions of every bounded time set. The result applies to self-similar SLE with stationary increments, chordal SLE in the half-plane, and chordal SLE in bounded piecewise $C^1$ Jordan domains. In the last case, the box-dimension conclusion holds under a positive-angle endpoint hypothesis. We also establish boundary-inclusive local H\"older continuity of every order below $1/d$ for chordal SLE in natural time and identify the exact local dimension $d$ of the natural occupation measure on compact time intervals.
item.dc:creator: Dapeng Zhan

item.title: Total variation bounds for Schr\"odinger--F\"ollmer sampling of boundary-vanishing densities
item.description: arXiv:2611.02542v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive total variation bounds for the Schr\"odinger--F\"ollmer sampler when the target density vanishes at the boundary of its support. This boundary behavior produces a terminal-time singularity in the drift near the boundary. We first prove a base estimate under a single quantitative hypothesis, finiteness of the relative Fisher information, without assuming boundedness or Lipschitz continuity of the drift. We then combine this estimate with a mixture regularization, thereby reducing the problem to determining the growth rate of the regularized Fisher information. For densities with an exact polynomial vanishing order on the boundary of a smooth bounded domain, we determine this growth rate and its leading constant. Orders above one yield the square-root rate in the number of steps, with a logarithmic loss at order one. For orders between one half and one, the rate exponent decreases continuously from one half toward one third. Finite mixtures of triangular kernel densities fall into the linear case.
item.dc:creator: Tatsuya Kaneko, Yumiharu Nakano

item.title: Invariance principle for long-memory linear processes under sublinear expectations
item.description: arXiv:2611.02610v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish an invariance principle for long-memory linear processes with power-law coefficients under sublinear expectations. Under truncated-moment and capacity-tail conditions, we construct these processes on a canonical space and prove weak convergence in continuous path space of their linearly interpolated, normalized partial sums. The limiting sublinear law is represented as an upper expectation over stochastic integrals with a fractional Brownian moving-average kernel and predictable volatility controls, driven by a two-sided classical Brownian motion. When variance uncertainty vanishes, the limit reduces to the classical fractional Brownian limit. The proof combines a multidimensional Rosenthal inequality, coefficient approximation, and the invariance principle for independent and identically distributed random variables to establish finite-dimensional convergence. Tightness follows from second-moment increment bounds. Uniform approximation on compact sets then extends the convergence from bounded Lipschitz to bounded continuous test functions.
item.dc:creator: Wang-Yun Gu, Li-Xin Zhang

item.title: Spectral Response Geometry for Liouville Brownian Motion
item.description: arXiv:2611.02641v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For Dirichlet Liouville Brownian motion associated with a subcritical Gaussian multiplicative chaos measure on a bounded planar domain, we study the response of finite spectral blocks under Cameron--Martin perturbations of the underlying Gaussian free field. For each fixed $0<\gamma<2$, we prove that, almost surely, all unordered eigenfunction-product measures in every finite simple spectral block are linearly independent. This strengthens the corresponding diagonal independence statement and implies surjectivity of the joint eigenvalue and eigenframe response map. We use this transversality to construct real-analytic local deformations that preserve a prescribed finite block of eigenvalues while varying its eigenframe. We then identify the least Cameron--Martin energy required to realize a given infinitesimal angular response, expressing it through a positive Schur complement of the response operator. Finally, on finite-dimensional Gaussian slices, we derive the conditional law associated with the local isospectral leaf and compare the induced slice metric with the full Cameron--Martin minimum. The results provide a local geometric description of spectral flexibility for Liouville Brownian motion.
item.dc:creator: Chunhao Cai

item.title: Generalized Wishart processes under nonlinear expectation
item.description: arXiv:2611.02728v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a theory of generalized Wishart processes within the framework of $G$-expectation, with $G$-Dyson Brownian motion and the $G$-Wishart process as two typical examples. In contrast to the classical setting, we show that $G$-Dyson Brownian motion may exhibit collisions and provide a sufficient condition ensuring the non-collision of the eigenvalues of generalized Wishart processes. We then derive the equations governing the high-dimensional limits of the empirical spectral measures under $G$-expectation, leading to the corresponding semicircle law for $G$-Dyson Brownian motion and Marchenko--Pastur law for the $G$-Wishart process.
item.dc:creator: Xinpeng Li, Yiran Mi, Jian Song, Shuzhen Yang

item.title: Sharp Injective Norm Bounds for Inhomogeneous Gaussian Tensors and Sparse Extensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.02813v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Euclidean injective norm of inhomogeneous random tensors with independent entries. For Gaussian tensors, we establish optimal two-sided bounds for the expected norm, with constants depending only on the tensor order. These bounds describe the interplay between variance accumulation along fibres and the contribution of the largest individual entries. In the matrix case, our result is consistent with the characterizations in~\cite{LVHY18}. We then extend the analysis to sparse Gaussian tensors with arbitrary amplitudes and activation probabilities. The expected norm is characterized by the expected largest absolute entry and the largest fibre standard deviation after truncating amplitudes at this scale. Our proofs combine geometric chaining with estimates for averaging over the random support.
item.dc:creator: Guozheng Dai, Ke Wang

item.title: McKean-Vlasov flights without moments: well-posedness, propagation of chaos and a critical threshold for law-dependent jumps
item.description: arXiv:2611.02859v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study McKean-Vlasov equations driven by an isotropic $2s$-stable L{\'e}vy noise, $s\in(0,1)$, whose solutions may have no finite mean, with coefficients that are Lipschitz with respect to a bounded Wasserstein-type distance. When the jump noise is additive, we prove strong well-posedness for every initial law and every $s$, without any moment assumption, and propagation of chaos at the rate $N^{-1/2}$ for kernel interactions. When the size of the jumps depends on the law, we prove the same results for $s>1/2$, and we show by an example that uniqueness fails for every $s<1/2$. The value $s=1/2$ thus separates well-posedness from non-uniqueness; the critical case itself remains open. These results answer, for stable noise, the question of uniqueness without moments raised by Jourdain, M{\'e}l{\'e}ard and Woyczy{\'n}ski and by Cavallazzi.
item.dc:creator: Houssine El Jeddaoui

item.title: High-order fractional linear differential equations do not describe stochastic processes with finite state space
item.description: arXiv:2611.02954v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The replacement of the classical derivative in the governing equation of a continuous-time Markov process with finite state space by a fractional derivative of arbitrary order $\alpha>1$ produces solutions that are mathematically incompatible with the theory of stochastic processes.
item.dc:creator: P. Van Mieghem

item.title: Local limit Theorem for Directed polymers in a random environment in the full weak disorder regime
item.description: arXiv:2611.02998v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For directed polymers in random environment, we provide a short and mostly self-contained proof of the local limit theorem in the full weak disorder phase, including the critical inverse temperature $\beta_c$. That is, the point-to-point partition function is well approximated by the product of two independent point-to-line partition functions (one starting from each endpoint of the system) multiplied by the simple random walk transition kernel. The approximation is valid in the $L^p$ sense for an optimal range of $p$. The result is new at $\beta=\beta_c$ and for $p>2$, and in all cases the proof is significantly simpler, technically and conceptually, than what can be found in the literature. As a consequence of the result we establish an invariance principle for the polymer measure with fixed end-point, valid for all $\beta \in [0,\beta_c]$.
item.dc:creator: Stefan Junk, Hubert Lacoin

item.title: Rigidity of the Peres-Vir\'ag class
item.description: arXiv:2611.03118v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Consider the hyperbolic Gaussian analytic function (GAF) \begin{equation*} F_{\mathbb{D}}(z)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty }\xi _{n}z^{n},\qquad |z|<1, \end{equation*} where the $\xi _{n}$ are independent standard complex Gaussian variables. Peres-Vir\'{a}g theorem tells that the distribution of the zeros of $F_{\mathbb{D}}(z)$ is provided by a Determinantal Point Process (DPP). We prove that $F_{\mathbb{D}}(z)$ is the only GAF whose zeros are determinantal with a Hermitian kernel, up to multiplication by a zero-free holomorphic function and a one-to-one holomorphic change of variable, with a \ non-degeneracy condition imposed to exclude trivial cases. The proof identifies a geometric property of GAF's with (local) determinantal zeros: the metric defined by the first intensity must have constant curvature $-4$.
item.dc:creator: Lu\'is Daniel Abreu

item.title: Near-optimal bounds for the critical 2d SHF and the delta-Bose gas
item.description: arXiv:2611.03191v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a near-optimal upper bound $\exp(\exp(CN^{1+o(1)}))$ for the $N$-th moment of the critical two-dimensional stochastic heat flow, improving on the bound $\exp(\exp(CN^{2}))$ of Gu, Quastel, and Tsai. Near-optimality follows from the lower bound $\exp(\exp(cN))$ of Ganguly and Nam. These estimates establish the exponential scale of the ground-state energy of the two-dimensional $N$-body delta-Bose gas predicted by Rajeev's conjecture, up to a vanishing error in the exponent. As a further step toward this conjecture, we derive, for each fixed $N$, a formula for the ground-state energy in terms of the bottom of the spectrum of a principal operator.
item.dc:creator: Xue-Mei Li, Te-Chun Wang

item.title: Free energy of the Hopfield model
item.description: arXiv:2611.03306v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We identify the limit of the free energy of the Hopfield model with independent symmetric Bernoulli patterns, for every temperature and loading ratio. A Hubbard-Stratonovich transformation reduces the problem to that of identifying the limit free energy of a bipartite spin glass with $\pm 1$ and spherical spins. One key difficulty is that the patterns, which become the coupling coefficients in the bipartite model, are Bernoulli instead of Gaussian, and the limit free energy is sensitive to the law of these coefficients. We show that the model is in fact equivalent to one involving Gaussian patterns and also subject to a finite number of Bernoulli random fields. We then solve this model by adapting the techniques recently introduced to identify the limit free energies of spin glasses with either $\pm 1$ or spherical spins.
item.dc:creator: Ayman Ali, Jeanne Boursier, Hong-Bin Chen, Fu-Hsuan Ho, Victor Issa, Jean-Christophe Mourrat

item.title: Sublinear Power-Law Growth of Level Set Diameters in Heterogeneous F-KPP Equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.03332v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every $\alpha\in(1/4,1)$, we construct a heterogeneous medium $\xi$ such that the diameter of the level sets of the solution to the F-KPP equation is of order $t^\alpha$ along a sequence of times tending to infinity. This is a natural continuation of a series of recent works establishing logarithmic lower bounds as well as linear asymptotics for the diameters of the respective level sets in random and deterministic heterogeneous media. Both results assume $\sup\xi > 2\inf\xi$; we also show that the diameter can diverge in the critical regime $\sup\xi=2\inf\xi$. A key ingredient is an estimate for branching Brownian motion with fixed time horizon $t$ and branching rate $1$ on the negative half-line and $2+t^{-\eta}$ on the positive half-line. This estimate exhibits a saturation transition: for $\eta<1/2$ the polynomial and logarithmic corrections to the extremal position depend on $\eta$, whereas for $\eta\geq1/2$ the extremal position becomes independent of $\eta$, up to an additive constant.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Drewitz, Pascal Hanigk, Lisa Hartung

item.title: Local Limit Theorems for Heavy-Tailed L\'evy Processes with Negative Drift
item.description: arXiv:2611.03385v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper establishes uniform local asymptotics for the first-passage time below zero and the stopped maximum of a L\'evy process with negative drift and a locally regularly varying L\'evy measure. We show that their probabilities of lying in distant intervals are asymptotic to the expected first-passage time multiplied by the corresponding L\'evy masses, uniformly over interval widths bounded away from zero, including unbounded intervals. Although the two local events have asymptotically equivalent probabilities, their conditional overlap vanishes for fixed-width intervals. Nevertheless, we establish conditional concentration of the first-passage time and stopped maximum around their deterministic linear relation on scales dominating the fluctuations of the centered process. We further prove conditional functional limit theorems yielding a single-step process with random jump time on the original time scale and a deterministic linear descent on the accelerated scale. Finally, we identify the joint limiting distribution of the unscaled pre-passage position and terminal overshoot, distinguishing continuous passage from passage by a downward jump.
item.dc:creator: Hao Wu, Wei Xu

item.title: Gaussian Products and an Order Dichotomy for Principal Ideals
item.description: arXiv:2611.03495v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We identify the algebraic principal ideal generated by a Gaussian product of two Hilbert--Schmidt operators. Its deterministic generator is obtained by multiplying the square tails of their singular-value sequences; in a fixed diagonal basis, one probability-one event gives the identity for all decreasing square-summable weights. For the induced operation on principal ideals, we prove an order dichotomy for arbitrary families of strictly positive probes. A family jointly determines every inclusion if and only if its tail stable-rank profiles have no common eventual upper bound. Equivalently, each prescribed countable input system admits one probe from that family reflecting all inclusions. If the condition fails, one common fibre contains a copy of $\mathcal P(\mathbb N)/\mathrm{Fin}$ preserving finite sums and intersections. Its generators are continuously parametrized and arbitrarily close in Hilbert--Schmidt norm, while their deterministic output ratios tend to one at any prescribed rate. The order dichotomy follows from a bound on all probes that lose one noninclusion and a separated block construction under a scalar tail budget. Further consequences include generic separation under every positive summable envelope and exact cardinal thresholds for joint detection and single-probe separation.
item.dc:creator: Guangqian Zhao

item.title: Stability of negative-regularity mixing and applications to stochastic fluids
item.description: arXiv:2611.03519v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider mixing for a scalar advected by random vector fields, such as solutions to stochastic fluid equations. Our main abstract result is that contraction in expectation of a negative Sobolev norm of the scalar (negative-regularity mixing) is stable under perturbations of the joint scalar-velocity process. We apply the result in three settings: mixing for a hyperviscous Boussinesq-type system where the scalar actively drives the velocity, mixing for a passive scalar advected by two-dimensional Navier-Stokes driven by smooth-in-time stochastic forcing, and a black-box proof that negative-regularity mixing implies enhanced dissipation.
item.dc:creator: Antonio Agresti, William Cooperman, Patrick Flynn

item.title: Local scaling limit of the four-dimensional uniform spanning tree
item.description: arXiv:2611.03582v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we prove that the uniform spanning tree of $\mathbb Z^4$, seen from the origin, converges locally to an infinite spatial Brownian Kesten tree: a Brownian spine onto which independent spatial Brownian trees are grafted at a constant rate. The convergence holds jointly for the intrinsic metric, the volume measure and the Euclidean positions of the vertices, after rescaling these quantities by suitable constant multiples of $n^{-1}$, $n^{-2}(\log n)^{1/3}$ and $n^{-1/2}(\log n)^{-1/6}$, respectively, under the local rooted spatial Gromov-weak topology. The rescaled space-time occupation measure converges to that of infinite canonical super-Brownian motion. We also identify the limiting law of the rescaled intrinsic-ball volume and obtain sharp first-moment asymptotics.
item.dc:creator: Runsheng Liu

item.title: Synchronization of Enriched Spin Glasses
item.description: arXiv:2611.03587v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that enriching a non-convex multi-species Hamiltonian by a uniform Ruelle probability cascade implies synchronization of the joint overlap array without an additional regularizing perturbation. In particular, we show that any limit point of the overlap array is a deterministic non-decreasing function of a uniform Ruelle probability cascade.
item.dc:creator: Franziska Engler, Justin Ko

item.title: Invariant probability measures on holomorphic functions on the unit disk
item.description: arXiv:2610.40057v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study probability measures on the space of holomorphic functions on the unit disk that are invariant under pre-composition by conformal automorphisms and give no mass to constant functions. We determine the slowest possible growth of functions supported by such measures. Let $M_f(R)$ denote the maximum modulus of $f$ on the hyperbolic ball of radius $R$ centered at the origin. We show that given a non-decreasing function $G:[1,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$, there exists an $\textrm{Aut}(\mathbb{D})$-invariant probability measure $\mu$ on $\textrm{Hol}(\mathbb{D}, \mathbb{C}) \setminus \{\textrm{constant functions} \}$ such that $\log^+ M_f(R)=O_f(G(R))$ for $\mu$ almost every $f$ if and only if $\int_1^\infty (R/G(R)) \, dR <\infty$. For the lower bound, we use a mass transport argument to show that almost every trajectory of the gradient flow of $\log |f|$ has finite energy. To establish sharpness, we construct holomorphic functions of slow growth on infinite Riemann surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Oleg Ivrii, Uri Kreitner

item.title: Inference in an interactive multi-type branching network
item.description: arXiv:2611.00152v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study statistical inference for a high-dimensional stochastic interaction model observed only through low-dimensional aggregate data. The model describes pairwise communication between $d$ individuals as a collection of mutually interacting branching processes with immigration, where activity on one directed pair may trigger subsequent activity in the reverse direction. The latent interaction counts are not observed. Instead, for each individual, only the total number of messages sent and received in each time slot is available.
