This aggregation gives rise to an inverse problem in which the parameters governing the latent pairwise dynamics must be recovered from substantially compressed observations.
item.dc:creator: Gunay Hasanli, Michel Mandjes, Jiesen Wang

item.title: How timing and mode of selection shape ancestral genetic contributions
item.description: arXiv:2611.00161v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We examine a population that evolves according to a biparental Moran model with two distinct types of individuals. Each individual's type is determined by the allele they carry at one biallelic locus, which is transmitted in a Mendelian way. This type influences the individual's mating preferences. We investigate two specific mating patterns: (i) where the type determines the level of attractiveness, and (ii) where the type dictates the level of homogamous choosiness. In both scenarios, one type has an advantage over the other. Assuming an initial proportion b of individuals are of the advantaged type, we give an explicit formula for the asymptotic proportion of the population's genome that originates from these advantaged ancestors under an infinite population size approximation. Our results enable a comparison of the relative strengths of homogamous choosiness, attractiveness, and viability selection in terms of genome transmission, and prove notably that viability selection is always more efficient than both forms of reproductive selection.
item.dc:creator: Juan Mardomingo-Sanz (SIMBA, IECL), Rapha\"el Tran-Thanh (LTCI, IP Paris), Camille Coron (MIA Paris-Saclay, INRAE), Diala Abu Awad (GQE-Le Moulon, INRAE)

item.title: Distortion of Random Max Filters over Reflection Groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.00305v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A max filter with Gaussian templates $a_1,\dots,a_D$ is a $G$-invariant map $\R^d\to\R^D$, where $G$ is a finite reflection group. As $D\to\infty$ its distortion converges a.s to the condition number of $M_G^{1/2}$, where $M_G$ is the second-moment matrix of a standard Gaussian vector moved into a fundamental chamber of $G$. We compute this limit exactly for the sign and dihedral groups, and show it grows as $\Theta(\sqrt d)$, $\Theta(d^{3/2})$ and $\Theta(k)$ for the sign, symmetric and dihedral groups of order $2k$. The symmetric case bound uses a lower bound on the covariance of order statistics. For any finite $G$ we also show that the infimum defining the optimal lower Lipschitz constant of a piecewise-linear $G$-invariant map is a minimum.
item.dc:creator: Efstratios Tsoukanis

item.title: Online carpooling against an oblivious adversary
item.description: arXiv:2611.00388v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In the online carpooling problem, edges on $n$ vertices arrive one at a time and must be oriented immediately, so as to keep the difference between the indegree and the outdegree of every vertex small. We give a randomized online algorithm which bounds the largest absolute difference over the first $T$ edges by $O((\log T)^{1/3})$ with high probability on every input sequence fixed in advance. This proves a conjecture of Kulkarni, Reis and Rothvoss and matches the known worst case lower bound. The algorithm keeps the law of the discrepancy vector dominated in the convex order by a Gaussian measure, and forces the endpoint with the smaller discrepancy to receive the edge whenever the two discrepancies are far apart. In the analysis we show that a vertex of discrepancy $D$ is preceded by a set of $O(D)$ vertices with total discrepancy $\Omega(D^2)$.
item.dc:creator: Yuhao Lei

item.title: Two-point concentration for graph classes admitting sparse vertex deletion
item.description: arXiv:2611.00437v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For fixed $p\in(0,1)$, we prove that the maximum number of vertices in an induced subgraph of $G(n,p)$ from a given class is concentrated on two consecutive integers, unifying and extending several earlier results. We require that the class contain arbitrarily large graphs and that every sufficiently large $k$-vertex member have a vertex of degree $o(k)$ whose deletion leaves a graph in the same class. This condition holds for empty graphs, trees, forests, planar graphs, graphs of bounded maximum degree, degeneracy or treewidth, graphs excluding a fixed complete bipartite subgraph (including graphs containing no cycle of length four), and many other graph classes.
item.dc:creator: Margarita Akhmejanova, Vladislav Kozhevnikov

item.title: Dynamic programming principle for controlled systems driven by fractional Brownian motions and related backward stochastic Riccati equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.00535v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This work aims to study the stochastic optimal control problems of controlled stochastic differential systems driven by both Brownian motions and fractional Brownian motions via dynamic programming principle. The stochastic Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation is obtained. Different from the classical case, the obtained stochastic Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation is a backward stochastic partial differential equation driven by both fractional Brownian motions and standard Brownian motions, whose solution is a pair of random fields. For linear quadratic optimal control problem this backward stochastic partial differential equation is explicitly solved by relating it to a backward stochastic Riccati equation.
item.dc:creator: Yuecai Han, Yaozhong Hu, Yuhang Li

item.title: Non-asymptotic analysis of SGLD with discontinuous stochastic gradients: a new route to portfolio CVaR minimization
item.description: arXiv:2611.00578v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Conditional-Value-at-Risk (CVaR) optimization is a fundamental tool in portfolio selection, yet its nonsmooth loss structure poses a challenge for the existing theory of stochastic gradient methods including associated Langevin algorithms. In particular, the positive-part loss and the softmax portfolio parametrization lead to stochastic gradients that need not be globally Lipschitz continuous, but rather discontinuous, where available non-convex stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics (SGLD) guarantees often exhibit an unfavorable exponential dependence on the problem dimension. In this article, we develop a non-asymptotic analysis of SGLD for a regularized CVaR portfolio optimization problem. We exploit the geometric structure of the CVaR objective to establish linear growth, convexity-at-infinity, and one-sided Lipschitz properties of the stochastic gradient without imposing density assumptions on the asset losses that are typical in previous works. Crucially, the constants appearing in the aforementioned structural conditions are shown to be independent of the number of assets. Moreover, we establish a convergence bound in Wasserstein-2 distance with rate $\mathcal{O}(\lambda^{1/4})$ and a finite-time guarantee for the expected excess risk. Our analysis, together with the dimension-independent constants in the structural conditions, leads to an excess risk bound that depends linearly on the number of assets. Numerical experiments with simulated Gaussian portfolios exhibit the predicted dimension dependence. Computational comparisons with alternative stochastic optimization methods further illustrate the practical efficiency of SGLD for the optimization problem under consideration. Finally, we extend the framework to a broader class of non-convex stochastic optimization problems with discontinuous stochastic gradients.
item.dc:creator: Yan Ding, Sotirios Sabanis, Ying Zhang

item.title: Large $N$ limit of the ratio of Lukyanov integrals
item.description: arXiv:2611.00662v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the large-$N$ asymptotics of ratios of Lukyanov integrals for fixed real coupling $b\geq1$. Our approach uses their biorthogonal ensemble structure and vector Riemann--Hilbert techniques. Under stated analytic hypotheses, we derive the logarithmic ratio through its constant term, which is expressed by a Fredholm determinant. The expansion is locally uniform in the real parameter $\alpha$ and is formulated separately for even and odd particle numbers. We verify the hypotheses for the correction defined by the physical ground-state thermodynamic Bethe ansatz. The relation to quantum-field-theoretic one-point functions is discussed separately.
item.dc:creator: Dong Wang

item.title: The e-Property for Quantum Markov Semigroups
item.description: arXiv:2611.00703v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $(\mathcal T_t)_{t\geqslant0}$ be a quantum Markov semigroup on a von Neumann algebra and let $\mathcal A$ be an invariant Feller $C^*$-algebra. We formulate the $e$-property on the full state space and show that its quantitative defect is equivalent, within an optimal factor two, to the Hausdorff measure of non-compactness of observable orbits. We develop Ces\`aro and Lip-norm criteria and a generalised Doeblin minorisation by a state-space contracting positive map, including finite-dimensional and measure-prepare factorisations. When every observable has the $e$-property, the Jacobs--de Leeuw--Glicksberg decomposition identifies the reversible Choi--Effros algebra and the norm-stable sector. Expected and decoherence-free subalgebras transfer the property under norm decay of the complementary dynamics, including infinite-dimensional ultracontractive and finite-index Pimsner--Popa regimes. Finally, we establish the full comparison hierarchy among ordinary, eventual, Ces\`aro and pointwise eventual equicontinuity notions, reinforced by matrix Jamison and homoclinic flow counterexamples. Projection-face criteria are treated in a companion paper.
item.dc:creator: Tomasz Kania, Mariusz Niwi\'nski

item.title: SAWs, trails, kites, patterns
item.description: arXiv:2611.00816v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A self-avoiding walk (SAW) on a vertex-transitive graph $G$ is a path that visits no vertex more than once; a trail is a path that traverses no edge more than once. The number of $n$-step self-avoiding walks (respectively, trails) starting at a given vertex has order $\mu(G)^n$ (respectively, $\mu_{\text{T}}(G)^n$), where $\mu(G)$ is called the connective constant and $\mu_{\text{T}}(G)$ is the trail constant. It is immediate that $\mu=\mu_{\text{T}}$ if $G$ either has degree $3$ or less, or is a tree. We prove a necessary and sufficient condition for the strict inequality $\mu < \mu_{\text{T}}$ if $G$ has degree $4$ or more and is not a tree, and in addition $G$ possesses a so-called height function. This condition is satisfied whenever the height function is transitive. The core of the proof is a pattern theorem for graphs possessing height functions, and this is achieved using an unpublished argument for ${\Bbb Z}^d$ by Hammersley, reported by Janse van Rensburg et al. (J. Stat. Phys. 85, 1996, 103--130). Some ancillary results are included concerning SAWs on the line graph of $G$.
item.dc:creator: Geoffrey R. Grimmett

item.title: Noise Stability on the Hypercube: Order $7/8$
item.description: arXiv:2611.00868v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a balanced Boolean function $f$ on the discrete hypercube, we study the $\alpha$-stability $\mathbb{E}[(T_\rho f)^\alpha]$, where $T_\rho$ is the Boolean noise operator and $0<\alpha<1$. Using the asymmetric Hellinger kernel estimates recently established by OpenAI, we prove that dictators minimize the $7/8$-stability in every dimension and at every correlation $0\le\rho\le1$. At interior correlations they are the only minimizers. As a consequence, dictators minimize the $\alpha$-stability for every $7/8\le\alpha<1$, maximize the $\alpha$-stability for every $1<\alpha<2$, and maximize the one-sided Shannon entropy stability $\mathbb{E}[T_\rho f\log T_\rho f]$. This resolves a conjecture of Li and M\'edard and strengthens the Courtade--Kumar conjecture in the balanced setting.
item.dc:creator: Lei Yu

item.title: Closed-Form Gaussian Mixture Representations of d-Dimensional Triangulated Domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.00922v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We derive a Gaussian Mixture (GM) representation of a full-dimensional subset of Euclidean space with finite volume from a finite simplicial triangulation in closed form. On each simplex, we replace the uniform probability density function (PDF) with a Gaussian PDF that minimizes the Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence, arriving at the information projection onto the family of Gaussian PDFs. By exploiting affine isomorphisms between simplices, the joint convexity and bijection invariance properties of the KL divergence, identities for Dirichlet PDFs, and a partition-of-unity argument, we establish a dimension-dependent but geometry-independent sharp upper bound on the global KL divergence between the resulting GM PDF and the uniform PDF on the original domain. Numerical examples illustrate the construction and demonstrate its potential in practical applications.
item.dc:creator: Ali Darijani, Benedikt Stratmann, Uwe D. Hanebeck, Ratan Bahadur Thapa, J\"urgen Beyerer, Nehal Afifi

item.title: Coefficientwise Hankel-total positivity from a universal cumulant lifting
item.description: arXiv:2611.01172v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Using probabilistic methods, we establish universal cumulant lifting criteria for Stieltjes and Hamburger moment sequences. In the Stieltjes case, we characterize coefficientwise Hankel total positivity after convolution with every initial moment sequence by requiring each once-shifted cumulant sequence to be Stieltjes. We also prove equivalence with the numerical moment property at every nonnegative intensity. In the Hamburger case, we use twice-shifted cumulants to obtain coefficientwise-positive leading Hankel determinants, a degree bound, an explicit highest-degree component, and drift invariance. We work with formal series and require neither exponential moments nor moment determinacy. We establish composition, binomial-convolution, and substitution results, and apply them to implicit equations and autonomous differential equations, tree and forest families, and lognormal compound-Poisson moments in a unified approach. From known moment sequences, we obtain general coefficientwise Hankel-totally positive families containing the classical Bessel, Lah, and Laguerre polynomials. We not only give new proofs of coefficientwise Hankel-total positivity of many combinatorial polynomials, but also prove coefficientwise Hankel total positivity for the component polynomials of functional digraphs confirming a conjecture of Sokal and establish fixed-shape Schl\"afli--Gessel--Seo polynomials positivity supporting another conjecture of Sokal.
item.dc:creator: Bao-Xuan Zhu

item.title: An Introduction to Financial Derivatives: Open Lecture Notes
item.description: arXiv:2611.01355v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: These lecture notes give a broad introduction to financial derivatives at the level of a Masters program in quantitative finance. Topics include forward and futures contracts, no-arbitrage bounds and put-call parity, the binomial model, the fundamental theorems of asset pricing, Brownian motion and It\^o calculus, the Black-Scholes model, the Greeks, variance swaps, local and stochastic volatility models including Heston, and static hedging of barrier options. Each chapter ends with exercises, and complete solutions, including Python code for the computational exercises, are provided in an appendix. The notes are open source: the LaTeX source is available at https://github.com/mattlorig/intro-financial-derivatives, and readers are invited to submit corrections and additions.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Lorig

item.title: An $\mathsf{FPRAS}$ for Mixed Volumes
item.description: arXiv:2611.01368v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We design the first fully polynomial-time randomized approximation scheme ($\mathsf{FPRAS}$) to estimate the mixed volume of $n$ arbitrary compact convex sets in $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ specified by weak membership oracles. This disproves a longstanding conjecture of Gurvits (2009). $\textbf{AI Disclosure}$ The main ideas were generated entirely by GPT 6 Astra. The purpose of this paper is to provide a human-written exposition of the algorithm.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoyu Chen, Kuikui Liu

item.title: Sharper Bounds for Graphical Two-Choice Allocation
item.description: arXiv:2611.01369v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In graphical two-choice allocation, vertices are bins, and each arriving ball must be placed irrevocably at one endpoint of a uniformly random edge. The objective is to keep the maximum-minus-minimum load gap small at every time. On cycles, endpoint-local monotone rules incur polynomial gaps at long time horizons, whereas global rules can achieve polylogarithmic gaps. We prove a joint exponential-moment inequality for the orthogonal contrasts of a binary partition tree, controlling all contrasts along a root-to-leaf path simultaneously. Applied to the Bansal--Feldheim strategy, it improves the gap on every $\kappa$-edge-connected $d$-regular graph from $O((d/\kappa)\log^4 n\log\log n)$ to $O((d/\kappa)\log^3 n\log\log n)$. We give an explicit strategy on the $n$-cycle with expected gap $O(\log^2 n)$ uniformly over deterministic times and exponential tails at each such time. An Euler-tour projection yields $O(\bar d\log^2(2M))$ for every connected graph with $M$ edges and degree-proportional capacities. For lower bounds, we introduce a stochastic cut workload: the expected largest normalized overload forced by the requests, plus an indivisibility term. For every online integral strategy, the supremum over time of the expected gap is at least one sixth of this benchmark. Regular rings of cliques attain $\Omega((d/\kappa)\log n)$ along an explicit family, improving the prior additive lower bound. With unequal capacities, the workload need not control the gap: one family has constant relative cut slack, bounded workload and gap $\Omega(\log\log n)$; another has workload at most $20$ but forces gap $\Omega(\log n)$ even for clairvoyant fractional allocations that remain irrevocable.
item.dc:creator: Obinna Okechukwu

item.title: Log-Sobolev inequality for the sine-Gordon model in the subcritical regime
item.description: arXiv:2611.01403v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a logarithmic Sobolev inequality for the massive two-dimensional sine-Gordon model throughout the subcritical range $0<\beta<8\pi$. For fixed mass, volume and arbitrary real coupling, the constant has a positive lower bound independent of the lattice spacing. When the dimensionless coupling is small, the lower bound is also uniform in volume and approaches the Gaussian constant as the coupling tends to zero. This extends the known range $\beta<6\pi$ and gives a rate of entropy decay for the reversible Langevin dynamics that remains positive as the cutoff is removed. The proof follows the Polchinski flow to a positive physical scale, where the Hamiltonian is a bounded perturbation of a uniformly convex one. For interactions invariant under constant field shifts, spatial differences bound their curvature by the gradient energy. For the oscillating part, we compare Gaussian integration with an average in which the original cosine phase fluctuates independently of the remaining variables. We estimate the comparison error at an intermediate scale, then differentiate the remaining Gaussian density. This preserves both phase damping and spatial decay without assuming bounds on second derivatives of the incoming local terms. The resulting strict gain between scales closes the estimates for every fixed $\beta<8\pi$.
item.dc:creator: Alexandru F. Radu

item.title: The Marvelous Meixner Polynomials: Second Kind, First Class
item.description: arXiv:2611.01422v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Meixner's classification asks which exponential generating functions can generate orthogonal polynomials. We follow the continuous Meixner family from this question to its moments, measures, and continued fractions. A beta integral and a bilinear identity establish positivity and orthogonality; Carlitz's Bernoulli and Euler constructions reveal further connections. Turning the parameter into a variable leads to rational orthogonality and Wall's fraction. We derive its Nevanlinna measure and unite the two spectral directions in a joint law with Cauchy marginals. Even finite pencils produce couplings with these exact marginals. Laguerre limits explain the gamma law governing joint extremes. Along the way, Meixner's scientific life, combinatorics, tangent numbers, and even zeta values illuminate the same structure.
item.dc:creator: Olga Holtz

item.title: Longest-Queue Policies in Dynamic Matching with Abandonments
item.description: arXiv:2611.01431v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study a dynamic two-way matching market in which agents of heterogeneous types arrive over time, wait to be matched according to a compatibility network, and abandon the system if their random patience expires. The decision maker collects match rewards and pays holding and abandonment costs, and seeks to maximize the expected net value over a finite horizon. We evaluate policies by their approximation ratio against a fluid benchmark, the optimal value of a linear-programming relaxation that upper bounds the expected net value of every policy. Under a general position gap (GPG) condition, which requires the unique optimal dual solution of this linear program to remain optimal under small perturbations of the arrival rates, we propose a longest-queue policy. The policy first uses this dual solution to identify a set of good match types and a set of critical agent types. Upon each arrival, it considers only good matches and matches the arrival to the critical partner with the longest queue subject to availabilities. In the high-volume regime, in which arrival rates are scaled by s, we prove that the policy attains an approximation ratio of at least 1-O(1/s) at every scale s >= 1 and every horizon T >= 1, so the ratio tends to 1 as s goes to infinity.
item.dc:creator: Siqi He, Yehua Wei, Jiaming Xu

item.title: The massive phase of the two-dimensional Heisenberg model is stable under small anisotropy
item.description: arXiv:2611.01532v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Polyakov predicted that the classical Heisenberg model on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ has exponentially decaying correlations at every temperature, and a proof of this has recently been posted. We show that the massive phase survives small anisotropy. For every inverse temperature $\beta$ there is $\delta(\beta)>0$ such that the $S^2$-valued model with couplings $\sum_iJ^i\sigma_x^i\sigma_y^i$ has exponentially decaying spin two-point functions, uniformly in finite subgraphs with free boundary conditions and in edge strengths up to $\beta$, whenever $|J^i-1|\le\delta(\beta)$ for $i=1,2,3$. For the easy-plane model with couplings $\sigma^x\sigma^x+\sigma^y\sigma^y+\lambda\sigma^z\sigma^z$ this shows that the onset of the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless phase, proved by Garban and de Montgolfier for every $\lambda\in(-1,1)$, moves to zero temperature as $\lambda\uparrow1$: in free-boundary limits, correlations decay exponentially for every $\beta\le c |\log(1-\lambda)|^{1/2}$. The physical prediction is of order $|\log(1-\lambda)|$. The same holds for aligned single-ion anisotropy, which includes a confining potential $\varepsilon\sum(\sigma^z)^2$, and for nearly isotropic $O(n)$ models with $n\ge3$. The proof keeps the sign-cluster argument of the isotropic proof, using Ginibre's correlation inequality for anisotropic planar energies, and uses the rotation symmetry only on one finite annulus, where the anisotropy is a bounded perturbation of the Hamiltonian.
item.dc:creator: Yan Ru Pei

item.title: Smoothed analysis of stability radii for the assignment problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.01584v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Every linear program can tolerate small changes to its costs and still yield a solution of the original problem. The size of this tolerance measures how robust an optimal decision is to noise or numerical error, and how much regularization the problem can support. Classical sensitivity analysis can determine this tolerance only from an optimal solution. This paper provides a priori lower bounds on two measures of this tolerance -- the optimality gap and the $\infty$-norm stability radius -- for the $n$-by-$n$ linear assignment problem over the Birkhoff polytope. The bounds derive from a smoothed analysis, which adds Gaussian noise with standard deviation of at least $\sigma$ in every direction to an arbitrary base cost. At every fixed confidence level, uniformly over the base cost, both quantities are at least of order $\sigma/(n\sqrt{\log n})$. The radius bound is asymptotically sharp. Under isotropic noise, the worst case occurs when every assignment has equal cost, and in this case, a scaled stability radius converges in distribution to a standard exponential variable.
item.dc:creator: Michael P. Friedlander

item.title: Boundary Harnack principle for abstract supersolutions on uniform domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.01586v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop an axiomatic approach to the boundary Harnack principle on diameter-uniform domains in proper doubling metric measure spaces. Under critical-density and upper-contraction assumptions, we establish a scale-invariant one-sided boundary comparison between nonnegative supersolutions and positive solutions and H\"{o}lder continuity of quotients of positive solutions. Our framework does not require linearity or rectifiable curves. Applications include classical elliptic equations, spectral fractional Laplacians, harmonic functions on fractals, and Pucci operators.
item.dc:creator: Takanobu Hara

item.title: Sharp upper and lower bounds on the variance of U-statistics
item.description: arXiv:2611.01690v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a U-statistic with a symmetric kernel of any rank, we offer new upper and lower bounds on its variance, which are uniformly sharper than those established in the classical paper by Hoeffding (1948, Theorem 5.2). Our new bounds have strong optimality properties and can tightly describe how the variance scales with the degree of the kernel. As an application, we leverage our new upper bound to improve an existing Berry-Esseen theorem for the normal approximation of incomplete U-statistics based on Bernoulli sampling, in a computationally frugal regime where the computational budget is much smaller than the available sample size.
item.dc:creator: Kiarash Nikoo, Liqian Zhang, Dennis Leung

item.title: Uniqueness of SRB measures for stochastic differential equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.01725v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a dissipation stochastic differential equation (abbreviated as SDE), exponential ergodicity has been investigated a lot in a wide range of settings. In this paper, we prove that the Markovian measure $\mu$ determined by the unique stationary measure is also the unique invariant measure which satisfies the entropy formula. Consequently, the existence of an SRB measure is completely determined by the sign of the sample top Lyapunov exponent of $\mu$: if $\chi_\mu^1>0$, then $\mu$ is the unique SRB measure, whereas if $\chi_\mu^1\leq0$, then the SDE admits no SRB measure. As an application, we establish a dichotomy of SRB measures for the 2D additive-noise stochastic Hopf normal form within a shear parameter domain.
item.dc:creator: Zeng Lian, Jianhua Zhang

item.title: Singular Tracking of Fractional Brownian Motion under Proportional Costs
item.description: arXiv:2611.01727v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study adapted finite-variation tracking of fractional Brownian motion under quadratic loss and proportional adjustment costs. For $H\in(0,1)$, \[ V_\lambda(T;a,b,\sigma)\underset{\lambda\downarrow0}{\sim}\kappa_HT a^{(1-H)/(1+H)}(\lambda b)^{2H/(1+H)}\sigma^{2/(1+H)}. \] The positive long-run cell value $\kappa_H$ is unchanged by full past information. A bounded full-past reset correction yields finite-horizon bounds and continuity in $H$. The Brownian value is $\kappa_{1/2}=\frac12(\frac32)^{2/3}$. Coupling local paths with their filtrations gives a local limit, which we verify for Gaussian Volterra targets. Every asymptotically optimal control has the same leading tracking--variation cost split. Primal and dual bounds quantify the cell value. For $H<1/2$, we construct a positive-factor approximation and relate factor resolution to horizon length.
item.dc:creator: Alexandre Autran

item.title: Covariant Calculus and Hamiltonian Flows for Nonlocal Wasserstein Metrics
item.description: arXiv:2611.01979v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we study nonlocal metrics on smooth positive probability densities on a closed manifold, induced by symmetric jump kernels and density-dependent mobilities. First, we introduce the density-variation operator to express the density derivatives of the Dirichlet form and kinetic energy. Second, we construct density and velocity-field representations of the tangent space and prove their isometric equivalence. We use the generator's pseudoinverse to derive Levi-Civita connections and covariant differentials in both representations. Third, we establish mechanical Hamiltonian dynamics in both tangent representations; an action principle and Legendre duality identify the Hamilton--Jacobi and covariant Newton equations; smooth negative gradient flows admit a zero-energy Hamiltonian lift. Entropy diffusion, nonlocal mean-field equations, Keller--Segel dynamics, and a nonlocal Vlasov equation illustrate the resulting calculus. For geometric-mean mobility, the Hopf--Cole transformation of the nonlocal Schr\"odinger bridge system and the Madelung transformation of the nonlocal Schr\"odinger equation yield hyperbolic and trigonometric phase energies, respectively. At zero momentum, both recover the metric kinetic energy to second order.
item.dc:creator: Yuanke Chen, Jinqiao Duan, Qiao Huang

item.title: Rare Event Constrained Reinforcement Learning with Large Deviations
item.description: arXiv:2611.02055v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study finite-horizon reinforcement learning with a safety constraint on the probability of reaching a failure set. In contrast to the well-studied safe reinforcement learning literature, we consider problems where the probability of reaching the failure set is vanishingly small, but the consequences of reaching the failure set are catastrophic. Direct simulation and estimation of the optimal policy is naturally ineffective when the failure probability is extremely small. Moreover, on a real system the controller can only choose actions, and this is not enough to make failures frequent. In contrast to the rare event simulation literature, our goal is not to estimate the probability of the rare event occurrence, but to upper bound it such that the failure constraint is satisfied. Thus, instead of sampling failures, we use the large deviations principle. We define a damage variable that on exceeding a certain threshold indicates failure. We study the cumulant generating function (CGF) as its positive root provides an upper bound on the failure probability via Cramer's theorem. We extend this approach to Markov decision processes with hitting times through state-action CGFs, and give finite-horizon and state-dependent versions of the bound. The state-action CGFs do not depend on the policy and can be estimated from regular transitions, so the bound can be checked for any policy a priori. This gives a policy improvement algorithm in which every policy satisfies the failure constraint with high probability.
item.dc:creator: Rahul Misra

item.title: Graphs versus loopless digraphs with a given degree sequence, and convergence of uniformly random graphs at every density
item.description: arXiv:2611.02191v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a degree sequence d on n vertices with M edges, let G(d) be the number of simple graphs and D(d) the number of loopless digraphs with in-degree = out-degree = d. We conjecture that G(d) >= sqrt(D(d)) exp(-C n log(2+M/n)) for every graphical d, a single inequality across all densities, and prove it up to an extra factor log n: G(d) >= sqrt(D(d)) exp(-C n log n log(2+M/n)) for every graphical d. The proof compares pairs of graphs with Eulerian digraphs by alternately colouring closed trails; the failure of injectivity is measured exactly, shared edges cancel against 2-cycles, and parity is handled by merging trails and by a parity argument on Eulerian circuits of odd components. No asymptotic enumeration and no bound on the maximum-entropy multipliers is used. When the maximum-entropy edge probabilities lie in [delta, 1-delta], the same method gives the conjecture itself, G(d) >= sqrt(D(d)) exp(-C n log n / delta). Combined with the exact identity G(d) = exp(g*(d)) pi(d), where pi(d) is the probability that the maximum-entropy beta-model has degrees exactly d, and a van der Waerden-type bound for D(d), this shows that uniformly random graphs with degree sequence d are close in the normalized cut metric to their beta-model whenever M >> n log n log(M/n), at every density, with no tameness and no cap on the degrees. We also record the conjecture in the sparse regime and, with constant 1/2+o(1), in the dense tame regime, from the asymptotic enumerations of McKay-Wormald and Barvinok-Hartigan.
item.dc:creator: Behzad Mehrdad

item.title: On the Conditional Consistency of the Bootstrap
item.description: arXiv:2611.02243v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper focuses on the conditional consistency of the bootstrap. The target is the conditional law of a statistic given a common shock, and the bootstrap approximates it by the law of a resampled statistic conditional on the shock and the data. We call the bootstrap consistent if these laws are close in the Kolmogorov distance for almost every realization of the shock. The conditioning $\sigma$-algebras are allowed to be unrelated across sample sizes, and both the comparison law and the dimension of the data may vary with the sample size. We give sufficient conditions for consistency in this sense, show that they yield asymptotically correct conditional coverage for bootstrap quantiles, and provide a finite-sample bound on the coverage error. We also relate the Kolmogorov formulation to the merging of probability measures. The results are specialized to statistics depending smoothly on an estimator or on an estimated nuisance parameter.
item.dc:creator: Denis Kojevnikov

item.title: Spectral Gap Inheritance for Metropolis-Hastings with Reversible Proposals
item.description: arXiv:2611.02381v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study Metropolis-Hastings kernels whose proposal kernels are reversible with respect to a reference measure, and establish sufficient conditions for such kernels to inherit a nonzero right spectral gap from their proposal kernel. Our conditions require the importance weight of the target relative to the reference measure to be bounded above, but do not require it to be bounded away from zero. Our approach combines a localized Holley-Stroock argument, which yields a local Poincare inequality, with a Lyapunov drift condition. As our main application, we analyze the preconditioned Crank-Nicolson (pCN) algorithm for sampling from measures on a Hilbert space that are absolutely continuous with respect to a Gaussian reference measure. Under local boundedness and quasiconvexity assumptions on the potential, we establish a dimension-independent $L^2$-spectral gap for this Metropolis-Hastings algorithm, thereby covering cases in which the local Lipschitz condition used by Hairer et al. (2014) is not satisfied.
item.dc:creator: Minhyeok Kim, Vinayak Rao

item.title: Regularizing the Navier-Stokes Equations by One Noise Component
item.description: arXiv:2611.02557v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the three-dimensional incompressible Navier--Stokes equations on the torus with multiplicative It\^o noise which is driven by a single Brownian motion and acts only through the vertical velocity component. Such a noise is strongly degenerate: An infinite-dimensional part of the velocity field is not forced at all. We show that it nevertheless has a regularizing effect. For a linear noise, strong solutions whose initial data have no unforced part are global with probability tending to one as the noise intensity grows. For a suitable nonlinear noise, the same holds for arbitrary $\mathrm{H}^1$ data, together with smallness of the space-time $\mathrm{L}^6$-norm of the vertical velocity. As a deterministic counterpart, we give a self-contained proof that a quintic damping of the vertical component yields global regularity, and the same argument shows that, under the linear noise, blow-up can only occur if the vertical velocity leaves $\mathrm{L}^6_{t,x}$.
item.dc:creator: Felix Brandt, Igor Kukavica

item.title: Fine-Grained Complexity Across the Computational Phase Transition
item.description: arXiv:2611.02702v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: How does a computational problem transition from easy to hard? In the hard-core model, approximate counting and sampling are polynomial-time tractable up to tree uniqueness, but worst-case intractable at any constant relative distance above it unless $\mathsf{NP}=\mathsf{RP}$. We quantify the transition from polynomial to exponential mixing for classical Glauber dynamics. On $n$-vertex graphs of maximum degree $d\ge3$, at fugacity $\lambda=(1+\delta)\lambda_{\mathrm c}(d)$ with sufficiently small $\delta\ge0$ that may vanish with $n$, its worst-case mixing time has the form $\exp\{\Theta(n\delta^2/d)\}n^{1+\Theta(1)}$. The upper bound is degree-uniform, and the matching lower bound holds for every fixed $d$. Annealing gives approximate counting with the same running-time upper bound at fixed accuracy. For general sampling and counting algorithms, we establish a robust fine-grained reduction from SAT without assuming a lower bound on SAT's running time. For any fixed $d\ge3$ and $0<\gamma<1$, a sampling or approximate-counting algorithm running in $\exp\{O((n\delta^2/d)^{1-\gamma})\}\operatorname{poly}(n)$ time along any one suitable inverse-polynomial distance sequence $\delta=\delta(n)$, yields a randomized SAT algorithm running in $\exp\{\widetilde O(s^{1-\gamma})\}$ time on inputs of binary length $s$. This power-saving transfer identifies $n\delta^2/d$ as the analogue of SAT input length for hard-core sampling and counting at relative distance $\delta$ above criticality: beating the Glauber exponent by a fixed power through any sampling or counting method would yield a corresponding power improvement for SAT. At criticality, we establish $O(\sqrt{n/d})$ spectral independence, optimal in $n$ at fixed degree, and degree-uniform Glauber mixing in $\widetilde O(n(n/d)^{1+1/(d-2)})$ time, improving the previous $\widetilde O(n^{4+4/(d-2)})$ bound.
item.dc:creator: Zhe Ju, Jingcheng Liu, Yitong Yin

item.title: All-Disorder Localization for the One-Dimensional Anderson Model with Power-Law Hopping
item.description: arXiv:2611.02724v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the one-dimensional random operator \[ (H_{\lambda,\omega}u)(n) = \sum_{m\ne n}\frac{u(m)}{|n-m|^r} +\lambda\omega_nu(n), \] where the random variables $\omega_n$ are independent and uniformly distributed on $[-1,1]$ (i.e., \mbox{$\omega_n\stackrel{\mathrm{i.i.d.}}{\sim}\operatorname{Unif}[-1,1]$}). For every $\lambda>0$ and $r>3/2$, we prove that $H_{\lambda,\omega}$ almost surely has pure point spectrum and admits an orthonormal eigenbasis $\{\psi_j\}$ satisfying \[ \sum_{n\in\bbZ}(1+|n|)^{2\tau}|\psi_j(n)|^2<\infty \qquad \text{for every }j\text{ and }0\le\tau<r-\frac32. \] These conclusions establish spectral localization, thereby rigorously confirming the prediction of earlier analytical and numerical studies in the physics literature, which identified $r=3/2$ as the marginal exponent.
item.dc:creator: Huajian Jiang, Yunfeng Shi

item.title: Correlators of the Jacobi Unitary Ensemble on a General Interval and Hurwitz Numbers
item.description: arXiv:2611.02795v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study correlators of the Jacobi Unitary Ensemble $\mathbf J(p,q,\alpha,\beta,N)$ of Hermitian matrices with spectrum in an arbitrary real interval $[p,q]$. For $(p,q)=(0,1)$, Gisonni, Grava and Ruzza expressed the large-$N$ expansion of the correlators $\langle\prod_j \mathrm{tr}\,X^{\lambda_j}\rangle$ through triple monotone Hurwitz numbers. We extend this genus expansion to arbitrary $p,q$ with $\alpha/N$ and $\beta/N$ fixed. Using the Frobenius characteristic map and the idempotent basis of the center of $\mathbb C[\mathfrak S_n]$, we also obtain an explicit formula for the Schur--Selberg type integral $\int_{(p,q)^N}\chi_\lambda(x)\,\Delta^2(x)\prod_a (q-x_a)^\beta (x_a-p)^\alpha\,\mathrm{d}^Nx$ in terms of irreducible characters of the symmetric group and content products. As consequences, we describe the zero-mean ensemble, and we recover, term by term in the genus expansion, the polygon-gluing formula for the Gaussian Unitary Ensemble in the limit $c_A=c_B\to\infty$. Structurally, passing from $[0,1]$ to $[p,q]$ leaves the hypergeometric weight of the associated 2D Toda tau function unchanged and only changes the specialization of its second set of times.
item.dc:creator: Matvey Sushkov

item.title: On some positivity properties of the Riemann $\Xi$ function
item.description: arXiv:2611.02944v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove strict log-concavity of the positive functions $\Theta$ and $\Lambda$ with one-sided and bilateral Laplace transforms $1/\xi(\tfrac12+\sqrt s)$ and $1/\Xi$, respectively, where $\Xi(z)=\xi(\tfrac12+iz)$. For either function, log-concavity is the P\'olya frequency property of order two (PF$_2$). Without assuming the Riemann hypothesis (RH), but using its published verification up to height about $3\cdot10^{12}$, we further prove that both densities are PF$_{k_*}$ for $k_*=1\,810\,540\,931\,075$. The proof views $\Theta$ as a small signed perturbation of a density that is PF of every order, with an error bound independent of the order, so the numerical check reduces to scalar inequalities. Since $\Lambda$ is a Gaussian mixture of $\Theta$, it inherits the same order. Conversely, a pole obstruction shows that if either density is PF$_k$, then every zeta zero lower than the $(k+2)$-nd lies on the critical line. Finally, we prove that if RH holds up to height $T>\tfrac12$, then $\Xi$ satisfies the generalized Laguerre inequalities $L_n[\Xi](x)\ge0$ of every order $n$ for $|x|\le T-\tfrac12$, extending the case $n=1$ of Csordas, Ruttan and Varga (1991).
item.dc:creator: Suvrit Sra

item.title: Strong Borel-Cantelli laws and clusters of visits for random intermittent maps
item.description: arXiv:2611.03010v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Near the neutral fixed point of an intermittent map, a single entrance into a small target can be followed by a long run of consecutive visits, so the number of visits need not follow its mean. We study targets $[0,u_n]$ for iid random compositions of Liverani-Saussol-Vaienti maps with a bounded parameter law that is regularly varying at its minimum $\alpha\in(0,1)$; this includes a single map. For $u_n=cn^{-g}L(n)$, where $c>0$, $0<g\leq1$ and $L$ is slowly varying, the visit count is almost surely asymptotic to its mean if and only if $\sum_n n^{-1}(nu_n)^{-(1-\alpha)/\alpha}<\infty$. Under the stationary law, the count divided by its mean converges to one in $L^1$ exactly when $nu_n\to\infty$. Thus clusters of visits separate these two modes of convergence.
item.dc:creator: Qihang Wang

item.title: Stochastic Homogenization of Schr\"odinger Equations with Exponentially Mixing Sub-Gaussian Potentials
item.description: arXiv:2611.03014v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the stochastic Schr\"odinger equation $ i\partial_t u_{\varepsilon} = H_{\varepsilon} u_{\varepsilon} $ with $ H_{\varepsilon} = -\Delta + V(x/\varepsilon) $, where V is a stationary ergodic sub-Gaussian field with exponential mixing. We establish the optimal algebraic error rate $ \varepsilon^{d/2} $ in $ L^2(\Omega; L^2_x) $ for every $ d\ge1 $, prove it sharp by a matching lower bound when $ \widehat{R}(0)>0 $, and upgrade the convergence of Zhang--Bal from convergence in probability to almost sure convergence. We further establish a Gaussian fluctuation central limit theorem with explicit covariance. The limiting fluctuation satisfies $ i\partial_t \mathcal{G} = (-\Delta + \bar{V})\mathcal{G} + \sqrt{\widehat R(0)}\,\dot W(t,x) $, a linear random Schr\"odinger equation driven by additive space-time white noise, where $ \bar{V} = \mathbb{E}[V] $ is the effective potential.
item.dc:creator: Fanfei Meng

item.title: Singular evolution of Gaussian measures under energy-critical and supercritical nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.03065v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider a family of nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations with odd-power nonlinearities and fractional dispersion in an energy-critical/supercritical regime. For a family of Gaussian measures supported on high-regularity spaces, we show that the flow immediately evolves these measures to ones that are mutually singular with respect to their initial distributions. In the cubic case, the threshold for singularity exactly corresponds to the energy scaling for the equation. In particular, we establish singular evolution of Gaussian measures under the flow of the energy-critical cubic NLS on the 4-dimensional torus.
item.dc:creator: James Coe

item.title: Density and Current Fluctuations for Run-and-Tumble Particles With and Without Interactions
item.description: arXiv:2611.03187v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study density and current fluctuations in a one-dimensional gas of run-and-tumble particles (RTPs), whose intrinsic velocities switch between two opposite values at a constant rate. We consider particles with and without pair interactions, including regularized Riesz gases, and also obtain corresponding results for Brownian particles. By linearizing the Dean-Kawasaki (DK) equations around a homogeneous stationary state, we compute density correlations and the variance of the integrated current through the origin. For repulsive Riesz interactions decaying as $1/|x|^s$ with $s>0$, this variance grows at long times as $t^{1/2}$ for $s>1$, but as $t^{s/(1+s)}$ for $0<s<1$. Starting from the same DK description, but retaining the Poisson statistics of direction reversals, we derive a macroscopic fluctuation theory (MFT) for RTPs with smooth pair interaction potential, which allows to compute the large time large deviation of the time integrated current. We show that, in the absence of interactions, the MFT saddle point equations can be solved explicitly using a generalized Cole-Hopf transform. This allows to recover and generalize previous results for the current distribution obtained by microscopic calculations, for RTPs with annealed or quenched step initial conditions. Beyond these distributions, MFT allows to compute the optimal density histories producing a prescribed current through the origin. We find that these density profiles, for both RTPs and Brownian particles, exhibit a nontrivial space-time structure. We also study stationary current fluctuations on an interval connected to reservoirs. Finally, we analyze the MFT equations perturbatively in the interaction. In both the infinite-line and reservoir geometries, we obtain explicit first-order corrections to the current generating functions for short-range interacting RTPs and Brownian particles.
item.dc:creator: L\'eo Touzo, Gregory Schehr, Pierre Le Doussal

item.title: On a Class of Non-Local Elliptic-Transport Systems in Score-Guided Probability Flow on $SE(3)$: Score-Singularity Resolution, Space-Time ADN Shift, and Markov Mean-Field Games
item.description: arXiv:2611.03278v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish mathematical foundations for optimal spatiotemporal vector fields governing continuous score-guided probability flows over bounded submanifolds $M \subset SE(3)$ on the Special Euclidean group $SE(3) \cong \mathbb{R}^3 \times SO(3)$. Modeling dynamic density evolution via a score-perturbed Lie-algebraic continuity equation under zero-flux boundary conditions, we resolve the non-local score drift singularity $s(g,t) = \nabla_{SE(3)} \log \rho(g,t)$ as $\rho \rightarrow 0^+$ via weighted parabolic flux dissipation bounds. Using left-invariant exponential group mollifiers, we derive boundary-preserving DiPerna--Lions commutator estimates tracking structure constants $\{c_{ij}^k\}$. Second, interpreting the optimality system as a 7D space-time elliptic operator $L_{7D} = -\Delta_{SE(3)} - \partial_t^2$ with zero-order corner compatibility on $\partial M \times \{0,T\}$, we establish Agmon--Douglis--Nirenberg $W_p^2(Q_T)$ shift estimates tracking Lie algebra constants, boundary geometry $\|\partial M\|_{C^2}$, and Ricci curvature $\|Ric_{SE(3)}\|_{L^\infty}$, yielding a full $C^\infty(\overline{Q}_T)$ Schauder bootstrap expansion. Third, we extend this system to non-cooperative Markov Mean-Field Games (MFGs) on $SE(3)$, establishing score-guided Nash equilibria via Schauder--Tychonoff fixed points. Crucially, the constant diagonal Ricci curvature $Ric_{SE(3)} = \mathrm{diag}(0,0,0,1/2,1/2,1/2)$ from $SO(3)$ induces a sharp Bochner--Weitzenb\"ock spectral gap boost $\lambda_1(-\Delta_{SE(3)}) \ge \lambda_1(-\Delta_{\mathbb{R}^3}) + 1/2 > 0$. This positive rotational curvature enhances the Lie-algebraic Poincar\'e coercivity constant, demonstrating that intrinsic group curvature stabilizes score-guided flows against dispersion and expands the critical Nash uniqueness horizon $T_{SE(3)}^*$ beyond flat Euclidean limits.
item.dc:creator: Pilhwa Lee

item.title: A height transportation approach to the quantitative Pr\'ekopa--Leindler inequality
item.description: arXiv:2611.03295v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a new, simpler proof of sharp stability for the Pr\'ekopa--Leindler inequality. In contrast to the main arguments from Figalli, van Hintum and Tiba~\cite{FigalliVanHintumTibaPL}, our proof hinges mostly on the sharp stability theory for the Brunn--Minkowski problem, developed by the same authors \cite{figalli2024BM}, and on the idea of using a height transportation approach in order to match level sets. As a by-product of our techniques, we are able to prove the sharp dependency on $\tau = \min\{\lambda,1-\lambda\}$ in the Pr\'ekopa--Leindler stability constant whenever one of the inputs is logarithmically concave, producing a new, simplified proof of two of the main results from~\cite{FigalliVanHintumTibaPL}. Finally, in the same fashion as Krist\'aly and P\^irvuceanu \cite{kristaly2026quantitative}, we are able to obtain new stability results for the Bakry-Emery log-Sobolev inequality and for the Talagrand inequality. Due to the sharpness of the inputs, these results are optimal in terms of exponents. We moreover show that the $L^1$ nature of the distance in such results \emph{cannot} in general be improved to any other $L^p$ distance, where $p>1.$
item.dc:creator: Jo\~ao Miguel Machado, Jo\~ao P. G. Ramos

item.title: Online Algorithms Cannot Find Isolated Perceptron Solutions
item.description: arXiv:2611.03397v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The binary perceptron problem asks for a length-$n$ sign vector in the intersection of $\lfloor \alpha n\rfloor$-many independent random Gaussian half-spaces. A striking feature of this model is strong freezing: at every constraint density $\alpha > 0$, all but a vanishing fraction of solutions are isolated -- $\Omega(n)$-far from all others, in Hamming distance. Such solutions are believed to be algorithmically inaccessible. Nevertheless, efficient algorithms find solutions at some constraint densities $\alpha$. One possible resolution of this apparent contradiction is that the solution space also contains rare well-connected structures, and that algorithms succeed by locating them. Gong, Huang, Li and Sellke (FOCS 2026) proved this for stable algorithms, by showing that such algorithms cannot locate isolated solutions with probability more than $\approx 0.84$. In this work, we study online algorithms, which receive the columns of the constraint matrix one by one and sign each irrevocably upon arrival. This is a widely used class of algorithms in discrepancy minimization, and it includes the algorithm of Jo and Lee (2026), which has one of the best provable guarantees for the binary perceptron. We prove that at any constraint density, any online algorithm outputs an isolated solution with probability $o(1)$. Our proof is based on the observation that the signs an online algorithm has already fixed can be completed to at most one isolated solution, so a successful algorithm must choose the unique correct sign for each of the last few columns. Using the exchangeability of these columns, we show that such an algorithm must match a suffix-parallel baseline, which signs each of them as if it were the next column to arrive. We then use an anti-concentration argument to show that such a baseline rarely produces a unique completion.
item.dc:creator: Shuangping Li, Gabe Schoenbach

item.title: Lee-Yang theorems for $q$-deformed oscillators and doubly-scaled SYK
item.description: arXiv:2611.03624v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that the vacuum partition function of the $q$-deformed oscillator \[ L_q(z):= \langle0|e^{zT_q}|0\rangle, \qquad T_q := \mathsf{a}_q + \mathsf{a}_q^* \] satisfies the Lee-Yang property, i.e., all zeros of $L_q$ lie on the imaginary line for all $q\in[-1, 1)$, proving the conjectures of Okuyama'23. Using the connection between $q$-deformed oscillators and the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) Hamiltonian in the doubly-scaled regime, we show that the annealed SYK partition function satisfies the Lee-Yang property in the thermodynamic limit, that is, all of its Fisher zeros are on the imaginary axis. As a result, we show that the quenched SYK partition function admits a zero-free strip of constant width with high probability, rigorously complementing the large$-k$ replica calculations of Zlokapa and Kiani'26. We show the imaginary-rootedness of $L_q$ by expressing $\varphi_q(z):= L_q(\mathbf{i} z)$ as a locally uniform limit of ``$q$-deformed'' matching polynomials and then showing that those $q$-deformed polynomials are real-rooted. This establishes that $\varphi_q$ is real-rooted, and in fact belongs to the \emph{Laguerre-P\'olya} class. The real-rootedness of the $q$-deformed polynomials yields novel log-concavity relations on the \emph{$q$-deformed matching moments} \[M_\ell(q):= \sum_{\pi\in\mathcal{P}_2(2\ell)}q^{\operatorname{cr}(\pi)}.\] We show the real-rootedness of the $q$-deformed polynomials by using the Touchard--Riordan formula to derive a partial differential equation relating their $q$-derivatives to their $z$-derivatives, and then analyzing the resulting motion of their roots.
item.dc:creator: Arpon Basu, Siddhant Midha

item.title: Construction of the 2D non-Abelian Yang-Mills-Higgs measure via stochastic quantisation
item.description: arXiv:2611.03640v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We provide the first mathematical construction of the non-Abelian Yang-Mills-Higgs measure on a two-dimensional torus by implementing Parisi and Wu's ``stochastic quantisation'' procedure. We use a specific gauge covariant (but non-Markovian) approximation to the previously constructed associated Langevin dynamics and develop a covariant paracontrolled calculus for it. This allows us to obtain short-time control over times that are much longer than what the cubic nonlinearity na\"ively suggests. When combined with the decay properties of the Yang-Mills-Higgs action under the deterministic gradient flow, as well as a quantitative measure of how the noise pushes the dynamic away from Yang-Mills connections, this is good enough to yield uniform-in-time bounds. We finally show that there exists a renormalisation under which our gauge covariant approximation converges to the Langevin dynamics (modulo gauge transformation) and that the latter is topologically irreducible and strong Feller. It therefore admits a unique invariant measure, providing the sought-after construction. Our construction is non-perturbative and works in particular for any fixed values of the coupling constants.
item.dc:creator: Bjoern Bringmann, Sky Cao, Martin Hairer, Wenhao Zhao

item.title: Stochastic Mechanics as a Gauge Theory
item.description: arXiv:0711.2978v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that non-relativistic Quantum Mechanics can be faithfully represented in terms of a classical diffusion process endowed with a gauge symmetry of group Z_4. The representation is based on a quantization condition for the realized action along paths. A lattice regularization is introduced to make rigorous sense of the construction and then removed. Quantum mechanics is recovered in the continuum limit and the full U(1) gauge group symmetry of electro-magnetism appears. Anti-particle representations emerge naturally, albeit the context is non-relativistic. Quantum density matrices are obtained by averaging classical probability distributions over phase-action variables. We find that quantum conditioning can be described in classical terms but not through the standard notion of sub sigma-algebras. Delicate restrictions arise by the constraint that we are only interested in the algebra of gauge invariant random variables. We conclude that Quantum Mechanics is equivalent to a theory of gauge invariant classical stochastic processes we call Stochastic Mechanics.
item.dc:creator: Claudio Albanese

item.title: Wasserstein Convergence Rate for Empirical Measures of Markov Processes
item.description: arXiv:2309.04674v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The convergence rate in Wasserstein distance is estimated for empirical measures of ergodic Markov processes, and the estimate can be sharp in some specific situations. The main result is applied to subordinations of typical models excluded by existing results, which include: stochastic Hamiltonian systems on $\mathbb R^{n}\times \mathbb R^{m}$, spherical velocity Langevin processes on $\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb S^{n-1},$ multi-dimensional Wright-Fisher type diffusion processes, and stable type jump processes.
item.dc:creator: Feng-Yu Wang

item.title: Sliced Wasserstein Geodesics and Equivalence Wasserstein and Sliced Wasserstein metrics
item.description: arXiv:2407.07219v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper will introduce a family of sliced Wasserstein geodesics which are not standard Wasserstein geodesics, objects yet to be discovered in the literature. These objects exhibit how the geometric structure of the Sliced Wasserstein space differs from the Wasserstein space, and provides a simple example of how solving the barycenter and gradient flow problems change when moving between these metrics. Some of these geodesics will only be H\"older continuous with respect to the Wasserstein metric and thus will provide a direct proof that Sliced-Wasserstein and regular Wasserstein metrics are not equivalent. Previous proofs of this were done for various cases in [2] and [5]. This paper, not only provides a direct proof, but also fills in gaps showing these metrics not equivalent in dimensions greater than 2.
item.dc:creator: John Seale Hopper

item.title: Additive processes on the real line and Loewner chains
item.description: arXiv:2412.18742v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper investigates additive processes with respect to several different independences in non-commutative probability in terms of the convolution hemigroups of the distributions of the increments of the processes. In particular, we focus on the relation of monotone convolution hemigroups and Loewner chains, a special kind of family of conformal mappings, on the upper half-plane. Generalizing the celebrated Loewner differential equation, we formulate an integral equation and the concept of ``generator'' for any Loewner chain of reciprocal Cauchy transforms. This generalization enables us to remove the assumption of the absolute continuity of Loewner chains which had been imposed in the literature. The locally uniform convergence of Loewner chains is then equivalent to a suitable convergence of generators. Using generators, we define homeomorphisms between the aforementioned class of Loewner chains, the set of monotone convolution hemigroups, and the set of classical convolution hemigroups on the real line. We also discuss similar homeomorphisms to free, boolean and anti-monotone convolution hemigroups on the real line.
item.dc:creator: Takahiro Hasebe, Ikkei Hotta, Takuya Murayama

item.title: A stochastic epidemic model with memory of the last infection and waning immunity
item.description: arXiv:2505.00601v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We adapt the article of Forien, Pang, Pardoux and Zotsa, on epidemic models with varying infectivity and waning immunity, to incorporate the memory of the last infection. To this end, we introduce a parametric approach and consider a piecewise deterministic Markov process modeling both the evolution of the parameter, also called the trait, and the age of infection of individuals over time. At each new infection, a new trait is randomly chosen for the infected individual according to a Markov kernel, and their age is reset to zero. In the large population limit, we derive a partial differential equation (PDE) that describes the density of traits and ages. The main goal is to study the conditions under which endemic equilibria exist for the deterministic PDE model and to establish an endemicity threshold that depends on the model parameters. The local stability of these equilibria is also analyzed. The endemicity threshold is computed for several examples, including models that incorporate a vaccination policy, and a local stability result is obtained for a memory-free SIS-type model.
item.dc:creator: H\'el\`ene Gu\'erin, Arsene Brice Zotsa-Ngoufack

item.title: Dispersion models on a circle: universal properties and asymptotic results
item.description: arXiv:2507.00737v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Consider a sequence of masses $m_0,m_1,...$ arriving uniformly at random at some points $u_0,u_1,...$ on the unit circle $\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$ (or on $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$, in the discrete version). Upon arrival, each mass undergoes a relaxation phase during which it is dispersed, possibly also at random. This process can model many physical phenomena, such as the diffusion of liquid in a porous medium. In the discrete case, it can model parking (related to additive coalescence and hashing with linear probing) in which the cars are permitted to follow random displacement policies. The dispersion policies considered in the paper ensure that at time $k$, after the successive dispersions of $m_0,\cdots,m_{k-1}$, the total covered region has Lebesgue measure $m_0+\cdots+m_{k-1}$. Furthermore, during the dispersion of a given mass, the covered domain increases continuously, except when it merges with another covered connected component (CC). We show a very general exchangeability property for the sequence of covered CC. Additionally, we demonstrate a universal spacing property between these CC, and a notable general result: if the $(u_i)$ are independent and rotationally invariant, then the number of free (not covered) CC follows a binomial distribution whose parameters depend solely on the number and total mass of arrived particles. Furthermore, conditional on the number of CC, the sizes of the free CC follow a simple Dirichlet distribution in the continuous case, regardless of the dispersion policy considered and the values of the masses. We also characterize the distribution of the occupied space. In the second part of the paper, we study the total cost associated with these models for various cost models, and establish connections with the additive coalescent. We also provide an asymptotic representation of the limiting covered space as the number of masses goes to infinity.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Marckert, Zo\'e Varin

item.title: Two-scale criteria for Poincar\'{e} and log-Sobolev inequalities with applications to Markov chain Monte Carlo
item.description: arXiv:2509.15410v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given a collection of distributions $\{P_{y}\}$ and a mixing distribution $\rho$ supported over $\mathbb{R}^{d}$, we propose new sufficient conditions under which the mixture / joint distribution satisfies a Poincar\'{e} or log-Sobolev inequality. We develop these sufficient conditions in a unified manner using the framework of $\Phi$-Sobolev inequalities (Chafa\"{i}, 2004). The conditions that we develop in this work are satisfied by a variety of Markov chains, and consequently allows us to characterise the evolution of these functional inequalities for iterates generated by simulating these Markov chains. As a result, we obtain an clean error analysis for estimating a broad class of functionals using Markov chain Monte Carlo strategies along these Markov chains.
item.dc:creator: Vishwak Srinivasan

item.title: On the Structure of Stationary Solutions to McKean-Vlasov Equations with Applications to Noisy Transformers
item.description: arXiv:2510.20094v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study stationary solutions of McKean-Vlasov equations on the circle. We establish an exact equivalence between solutions of the stationary McKean-Vlasov equation and an infinite-dimensional quadratic system of equations over Fourier coefficients, allowing explicit characterization of stationary states in a sequence space rather than a function space. This framework provides a transparent description of local bifurcations, their periodicity and resonance structures, while accommodating singular potentials. We derive analytic expressions for the emergence, form and shape (supercritical, critical, subcritical or transcritical) of bifurcations involving possibly multiple Fourier modes and connect them with discontinuous phase transitions. We also characterize, under suitable assumptions, the detailed structure of the stationary bifurcating solutions through leading small-amplitude coefficients for arbitrarily many fixed Fourier modes. At the global level, we establish regularity and concavity properties of the free energy landscape, proving existence, compactness, and coexistence of globally minimizing stationary measures, and identifying discontinuous phase transitions with points of non-differentiability of the minimum free energy map. We apply the theory to the Noisy Mean-Field Transformer model, where we show how changing the inverse temperature $\beta$ affects the geometry of the infinitely many bifurcations from the uniform measure. We also discuss how increasing $\beta$ motivates the study of approximate multi-mode stationary profiles as candidates for a separate metastability analysis; persistence times require additional dynamical estimates. Moreover, we determine the exact threshold $\beta_0\simeq2.447$ separating continuous and discontinuous phase transitions in this model. The same threshold marks the change of the first bifurcation from supercritical to subcritical.
item.dc:creator: Krishnakumar Balasubramanian, Sayan Banerjee, Philippe Rigollet

item.title: An explicit formula for the limit of the heat kernel measures on the spheres embedded in $\mathbb {R}^\infty$
item.description: arXiv:2510.25855v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that the heat kernel measures based at the north pole of the spheres $S^{N-1}(\sqrt N)$, with a properly scaled radius $\sqrt N$ and adjusted center, in the sense of finite-dimensional marginals, to a Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^\infty$. In particular, in the direction of the base point, the variance of this limiting measure is $1-e^{-t}-te^{-t}$, and in the orthogonal directions, the variance is $1-e^{-t}$.
item.dc:creator: Minh-Luan Doan, Evan O'Dorney

item.title: A modified Consensus-Based Optimization model: consensus formation and uniform-in-time propagation of chaos
item.description: arXiv:2511.19116v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a modified CBO model based on a regularized Gibbs weight. For each fixed temperature and regularization parameter, the regularized weight yields a configuration-independent lower bound on the denominator of the consensus map, thus a quantitative analysis without an upper bound on the objective function or cutoff in the noise. We first prove large-time consensus for the finite-particle system: above an explicit stability threshold, every particle converges exponentially to a common random limit. This consensus mechanism does not require the $C^2$ condition used in the direct weighted-energy argument. We next prove uniform-in-time propagation of chaos: we derive quantitative bounds for the finite-particle consensus point from finite-time concentration estimates for the mean-field law, with explicit approximation and large-time tail errors. The synchronous-coupling estimate also gives a quantitative comparison between the random particle consensus point and the deterministic mean-field consensus point. We also quantify the regularization error in the quantitative Laplace principle, making the effect of the additive regularization explicit. A direct weighted-energy estimate is obtained under stronger $C^2$ assumptions. Furthermore, we give a stopped quadratic stability estimate with the actual Gibbs denominator. Under the weak-landscape condition, full support of the initial law, and local nondegeneracy of the minimizer, we prove a high-probability finite-particle global-optimization theorem for any fixed $\lambda>\sigma^2$. The proof combines an affine-flow local-mass estimate, finite-time mean-field entrance, ordinary finite-horizon propagation of chaos, and an $\alpha$-independent convex trapping energy near the minimizer.
item.dc:creator: Young-Pil Choi, Seungchan Lee, Sihyun Song

item.title: Peng's Maximum Principle for Stochastic Delay Differential Equations of Mean-Field Type
item.description: arXiv:2512.00934v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We extend Peng's maximum principle to the case of stochastic delay differential equations of mean-field type. More precisely, the coefficients of our control problem depend on the state, on the past trajectory and on its expected value. Moreover, the control enters the noise coefficient and the control domain may be non-convex. Our approach is based on a lifting of the state equation to an infinite dimensional Hilbert space that removes the explicit delay in the state equation. The main ingredient in the proof of the maximum principle is a precise asymptotic for the expectation of the first order variational process, which allows us to neglect the corresponding second order terms in the expansion of the cost functional.
item.dc:creator: Giuseppina Guatteri, Federica Masiero, Lukas Wessels

item.title: Convergence rate of empirical measures in the subspace robust Wasserstein distance
item.description: arXiv:2512.04462v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We obtain an estimate for the expected subspace robust 2-Wasserstein distance between any probability measure with a finite q-th moment (q>2) defined on a separable Hilbert space, and its empirical distribution from $n$ i.i.d. samples.
item.dc:creator: Dakshesh Vasan

item.title: Pathwise uniqueness by noise for singular stochastic PDEs
item.description: arXiv:2512.17736v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Uniqueness for stochastic PDEs with drift in differential form is a main open problem in the recent literature on regularisation by noise. This paper establishes a self-contained theory in the framework of stochastic evolution equations on separable Hilbert spaces and provides a first result to address such an issue, in the direction of both pathwise and weak uniqueness, as well as continuous dependence on the initial data. The singularity of the drift allows to achieve novel uniqueness results for several classes of examples, ranging from fluid-dynamics to phase-separation models.
item.dc:creator: Davide Addona, Davide Bignamini, Carlo Orrieri, Luca Scarpa

item.title: Discrete Gaussian Free Field via Hadamard's formula
item.description: arXiv:2603.14776v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish a discrete Hadamard variational formula for Green operators on weighted graphs along an increasing family of subgraphs. The increment of the Green operator factors through harmonic extension from the newly added layer and the positive square root of its boundary Green operator. This gives a dimension-free decomposition of the Green kernel and an associated isometric Hadamard operator. As an application, the discrete Gaussian free field is constructed by successively adding independent harmonically extended Gaussian contributions. The formulation uses only the graph structure and its conductances, without smoothness assumptions. For nested square-lattice approximations of smooth planar domains, we also prove convergence of the growing fields in finite-dimensional distributions and convergence of the integrated Hadamard increments as Green-operator forms.
item.dc:creator: Haakan Hedenmalm, Pavel Mozolyako, Daniil Panov

item.title: Exact solution of the ruin problem in the Cram\'er--Lundberg with proportional investments and the limits of applicability of the power-law asymptotics
item.description: arXiv:2604.08745v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Cram\'er-Lundberg model with exponential claims and proportional investment is solved exactly: the integro-differential equation for the survival probability reduces to a doubly confluent Heun equation, yielding an explicit solution in terms of Heun functions, a verification theorem, and a qualitative analysis of ruin probability versus investment share.
item.dc:creator: Platon Promyslov, Maxim Romanov, Goluba Yurieva

item.title: Uniqueness and Mixing in the Low-Temperature Random-Cluster Model on Trees and Random Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2604.20693v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the random-cluster model on trees and treelike graphs at low temperatures. This is a model of dependent percolation parametrized by an edge probability $p\in (0,1)$ and a clustering weight $q\in [1,\infty)$, generalizing independent Bernoulli percolation ($q=1$) and closely related to the classical ferromagnetic Ising and Potts spin systems at integer $q$. For $q>2$, approximately sampling from this model on graphs of degree at most $\Delta$ is computationally hard. At parameter $p$ below the tree uniqueness threshold $p_{\mathsf{u}}(q,\Delta)$, it is expected that sampling is easy and local Markov chains mix rapidly on all bounded degree graphs. On typical graphs (e.g., random regular graphs), the same is predicted at $p > p_{\mathsf{s}}(q,\Delta)$, where $p_{\mathsf{s}}(q,\Delta)$ is a second uniqueness transition point on the $\Delta$-regular wired tree. Our first result establishes this non-uniqueness/uniqueness phase transition at $p_{\mathsf{s}}(q,\Delta)$ for all $q$ on the infinite $\Delta$-regular wired tree, resolving a conjecture of H{\"a}ggstr{\"o}m (1996). For this, we establish weak spatial mixing at $p>p_{\mathsf{s}}(q,\Delta)$ under sufficiently wired boundary conditions. We use this understanding of decay of correlations to show that on the wired tree on $n$ vertices, whenever $q>1$ and $p>p_{\mathsf{s}}(q,\Delta)$, the mixing time of random-cluster Glauber dynamics is a near-optimal $n^{1+o(1)}$. We then extend these results on spatial and temporal mixing from the tree to treelike geometries with mostly wired boundaries and use them to show that the random-cluster Glauber dynamics mix rapidly on the random $\Delta$-regular graph for all $p>p_{\mathsf{s}}(q,\Delta)$ as long as $q \ge C \log \Delta$, providing an efficient sampling algorithm for both the random-cluster and Potts models in this context.
item.dc:creator: Antonio Blanca, Reza Gheissari, Heehyun Park, Xusheng Zhang

item.title: Logarithmic scaling of selective sweep curves: from tents to houses
item.description: arXiv:2605.10617v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: One of the classical results of mathematical population genetics states that the frequency of a beneficial mutant's offspring, on its way to fixation in a large population, looks like a logistic curve. A logarithmic scaling (both in height and time) of these selective sweep curves leads (in the case of strong selection) to a tent-like shape in the large population limit: First the logarithmic frequency of the mutant increases linearly from 0 to 1, then that of the former resident decreases from 1 to 0. For moderate selection the logarithmic frequencies develop (in the large population limit) a jump at the beginning/the end of the sweep, which takes the shape of the tent into that of a house. Our main result (proved for the Moran model) assesses the regularity of this convergence in the large population limit: It is uniform in the house's roof (phases of linear growth and decline) and "Skorokhod $M_1$" in the house's walls (closely around the jumps). Apart from interest in its own right, we anticipate that this result and the proof techniques will be instrumental for extending the description of clonal interference by Poissonian interacting trajectories (as it was done in Hermann et al. (2024) for strong selection) also to moderate selection.
item.dc:creator: Florin Boenkost, Felix Hermann, Andr\'as T\'obi\'as, Anton Wakolbinger

item.title: Excursion-dependent inverse-subordinator time changes of regenerative processes: Excursion structure and multiscale occupation-time limits
item.description: arXiv:2605.23659v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study an excursion-dependent generalization of inverse-subordinator time changes for recurrent regenerative processes. Subordinators from an independent family are assigned to measurable classes of excursions and to the distinguished state at which the process is regenerative, and the random clock is constructed from the corresponding occupation times. Although the time-changed process is not necessarily regenerative or Markovian, we show that its transformed excursion point process is again Poisson and is obtained from the original excursion point process by a marking-and-mapping procedure. We also identify the transformed stagnancy component, on the original local-time scale, as a subordinator independent of this point process. We use this representation to study occupation- and waiting-time asymptotics. Under regular variation assumptions on the tails of the L\'evy measures of the cumulative excursion lifetimes and stagnancy components, we prove a multiscale joint occupation-time limit theorem, including generalized arcsine laws and Darling--Kac-type limits. We further obtain joint scaling limits for the last and next visit times to the distinguished state.
item.dc:creator: Kosuke Yamato

item.title: The existence of invariant sublinear expectations for $G$-SDEs
item.description: arXiv:2606.15203v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study the existence of invariant sublinear expectations of Markovian semigroups on sublinear expectation spaces. To achieve this, we establish a complete metric space of sublinear expectations, on which we extend Harris' method to the nonlinear setting on the convergence of sublinear semigroups. We then explore two cases of $G\text{-}$diffusions by studying the Lyapunov function and the local Doeblin condition.
