One is the $G\text{-}$Brownian motion on the unit circle which is the case studied in Feng and Zhao(2021), but with the new method. Another is the multidimensional $G\text{-}$SDEs on the whole space $\mathbb{R}^d$. We establish, for the first time in the literature, the existence of the invariant sublinear expectation for $G\text{-}$SDEs under the non-degenerate and weakly dissipative assumption. For this, we prove that for a class of $G\text{-}$SDEs, the $G\text{-}$expectation can be represented as the supremum of the semigroup of a family of SDEs, of which the regularity is obtained by considering { oscillations and coupling of the nonlinear Markovian semigroup,} and the Denis-Hu-Peng representation for the distribution of $G\text{-}$Brownian motions.
item.dc:creator: Danyang Zhao, Huaizhong Zhao

item.title: Fluctuations of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick free energy at critical temperature
item.description: arXiv:2607.02172v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick spin glass model at the critical inverse temperature $\beta = 1$ with zero external field. We prove that the free energy $F_N = F_{N,\beta=1}$ of this model has variance \[ \mathrm{Var}(F_N) = \frac16 \log N + O(1)\,, \] confirming a physics prediction of Aspelmeier \cite{aspelmeier2008free}, and that the centered and scaled $F_N$ satisfies a Gaussian CLT. We also identify the critical two-replica overlap scale, proving \[ \mathbb{E} \langle R_{1,2}^2\rangle \asymp N^{-2/3}\,, \] as conjectured by Talagrand \cite{talagrand2011mean2}, together with a uniform exponential moment bound for $N^{1/3} |R_{1,2}|$. The key input is a critical reweighted moment method, in the spirit of the ``small subgraph conditioning'' technique from probabilistic combinatorics, but capable of capturing diverging fluctuations. Through this reweighting, we relate the critical SK model to the BBP critical edge, which determines the overlap and fluctuation scales.
item.dc:creator: Hang Du, Brice Huang

item.title: A multi-player optimal stopping game based on a spider Brownian motion
item.description: arXiv:2607.22416v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper studies a multi-player non-zero-sum optimal stopping game driven by a spider Brownian motion. We study a specific, tractable family of games and the focus is on the existence and uniqueness of subgame-perfect Nash equilibria (SPNE). We begin by analyzing the two-player setting, in which the underlying process is a skew Brownian motion, and establish sufficient conditions for the existence of an SPNE. We then derive sufficient conditions for the uniqueness of the SPNE in the symmetric case, (where the skew Brownian motion reduces to a standard Brownian motion and both players have the same payoff structures). We also give examples which show that there can be multiple SPNE or no SPNE. We then extend the framework to the multi-player setting and provide sufficient conditions for the existence of an SPNE in this more general setting with a spider Brownian motion.
item.dc:creator: David Hobson, Jingfei Liu

item.title: A Two-regime Khintchine Inequality and an Improved Bound on the Degree-1 Fourier Weight for Linear Threshold Functions
item.description: arXiv:2608.27908v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Khintchine inequality provides a lower bound on the expected absolute value of a weighted sum of independent Rademacher random variables. In the classical setting, when the coefficient vector has unit Euclidean norm, this lower bound is a constant, with equality attained only by a simple family of extremal configurations. A refinement due to De, Diakonikolas, and Servedio, referred to as the \emph{linear Khintchine inequality} in this work, strengthens this estimate by establishing a lower bound that depends linearly on the distance of the coefficient vector from the extremal set. In this paper, we present a refined analysis of this dependence on the weight vector. Our results reveal a phase transition in the rate of improvement: when the dimension exceeds six, the lower bound undergoes an abrupt change as the weight vector deviates from the minimizer. Additionally, we improve the slope constant in linear Khintchine inequality. As a consequence, we establish an improved lower bound on the degree-1 Fourier weight for linear threshold functions $\mathbf W^{\leq1}[f]\geq0.55100929$, marking progress towards a conjecture of Benjamini, Kalai, and Schramm.
item.dc:creator: Xuan Fang, Tianyu Wang

item.title: Diffusions with critical divergence-free drifts: Varadhan asymptotics and path-law singularity
item.description: arXiv:2610.06341v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the Euclidean Varadhan formula (EVF) and path laws for diffusions with critical divergence-free drifts in dimension $d\geq2$. For drifts given by smooth bounded skew-symmetric stream matrices, we prove a quantitative lower bound under a sector condition with a lower-order term. Its constants depend only on the dimension and the sector condition data. By approximation, the locally uniform Euclidean lower bound holds for all divergence-free $L^\infty_t{\rm BMO}^{-1}_x$ drifts. However, a time-dependent counterexample shows that EVF can fail even for a drift in $L^\infty_tL^d_x$. A complementary upper bound is given under a structural decomposition condition. In particular, for every time-independent $L^{d,\infty}$ drift (without any smallness assumption), and the decoupled diffusion associated with the two-dimensional vorticity equation, the EVF holds. Finally, we construct a time-independent $L^d$ drift whose SDE has a unique strong solution from the origin and whose path law is mutually singular with the corresponding driftless Brownian law. The same diffusion satisfies EVF, showing that Brownian short-time endpoint costs can persist despite singularity of the path law.
item.dc:creator: Jintao Feng, Guohuan Zhao

item.title: Subspace Uncertainty and Sharp Sampling Thresholds on the Boolean Cube
item.description: arXiv:2610.12358v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a known finite-dimensional model subspace, classical Gaussian regression theory guarantees that least squares eventually attains the parametric rate, with prediction error scaling as the subspace dimension divided by the sample size. Yet subspaces with the same number of unknown coefficients can require very different sample sizes to reach this regime. For subspaces of polynomials on the Boolean cube, a fundamental question is how restrictions on degree and ambient dimension jointly determine this threshold. Our main result sharply characterizes the worst-subspace minimax sample threshold over a substantial parameter range, revealing an exponential dependence on degree and precisely quantifying the joint effects of degree, ambient dimension, and subspace dimension. A small modification of our lower-bound construction reveals a strong separation: a single subspace can admit noiseless recovery with optimal sample complexity independent of degree, yet require essentially the worst-case sample size, exponential in degree, to attain the noisy parametric rate. To establish the sampling lower bound, we sharpen the Polyanskiy-Samorodnitsky uncertainty principle (J. Funct. Anal., '19) to uniformly optimal precision and extend its concentration guarantee to large subspaces in which every function concentrates most of its energy on one shared Hamming ball. The sampling upper bound follows from the sharp moment bound of Kirshner and Samorodnitsky (IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory, '21) combined with empirical-process bounds.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Weinberger

item.title: Asymptotic Error Distributions for Euler-Maruyama Schemes with Additive Semimartingale Noise
item.description: arXiv:2610.20225v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish a joint stable limit theorem for integrated discretization errors of finite-dimensional c\`adl\`ag semimartingales whose predictable characteristics are absolutely continuous in time and satisfy a pathwise integrability condition. The normalized integrated error, evaluated on the discretization grid, converges stably jointly with the discretized semimartingale in the vector-valued Skorokhod $J_1$-topology. No martingale representation property is assumed. We apply this theorem to the Euler--Maruyama scheme for stochastic differential equations with additive semimartingale noise. For a $C^1$ drift with locally Lipschitz derivative and a nonexplosive solution, the grid-point error normalized by n converges stably jointly with the discretized driver. The limiting error solves a linear integral equation with an explicit inhomogeneous term involving the driver, an auxiliary Brownian motion, and independent uniform marks attached to the jumps. We also obtain the same limit under two alternative sets of assumptions allowing less regular drifts, based on small-jump integrability or smoothing estimates for L\'evy semigroups. For continuous drivers, the continuous-time error converges stably in the uniform topology.
item.dc:creator: Mikio Hirokane

item.title: Gaps between roots in ballistic deposition on a strip: linear variance, Gaussian limits and a Poisson regime
item.description: arXiv:2610.21094v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Mansour, Rastegar and Roitershtein studied the \emph{roots} of ballistic deposition on a cyclic strip of $K$ sites, namely the sites that receive a particle at height one, and the number $D_{i,K}$ of pairs of consecutive roots at distance $i+1$. They computed the first two moments of $D_{i,K}$ for $i\le7$. They conjectured that for every $i$ the mean and the variance are exactly linear in $K$, that $D_{i,K}$ satisfies a central limit theorem, and that the standardized vector $(D_{i,K})_{i\ge1}$ converges to a Gaussian process. We prove these conjectures. The key observation is that the roots are exactly the valleys of a uniformly random circular arrangement, so that $D_{i,K}$ counts occurrences of a family of consecutive patterns. We determine sizes from which the moments are exactly linear; the size for the mean is sharp for every $i$, and those for the second moments cannot be lowered in any case we checked. We give closed forms for the variance constants and for the limiting covariance; the mean constants agree with a known distribution of distances between surface peaks. The reduction and the exact moment formulas are formalized in Lean~4 with Mathlib. We also prove a Wasserstein bound of order $(\mathbb{E} D_{i,K})^{-1/2}$ that is uniform in $i$, and a local limit theorem. Finally we describe the limit completely when $i$ grows with $K$: it is degenerate, Poisson or Gaussian according as $\mathbb{E} D_{i,K}$ tends to zero, to a positive constant, or to infinity.
item.dc:creator: Mateo Matijasevick

item.title: Higher-order sum rules for zeros of the planar Gaussian entire function
item.description: arXiv:2610.23697v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For each fixed integer $k\ge2$, we prove that integrating one coordinate of the truncated correlation of order $k$ for zeros of the planar Gaussian entire function (GEF) gives $-(k-1)$ times the truncated correlation of order $k-1$. The integral converges absolutely, and the identity holds pointwise, including at coincident fixed coordinates by continuous extension. This answers the marginal-identity part of Krishnapur and Yogeshwaran's question for the planar GEF. We also prove a general criterion for simple point processes: under local moment and absolute integrability assumptions, the identities hold almost everywhere if there are compactly supported cutoffs between zero and one, eventually equal to one on each compact set, whose linear statistics have variances tending to zero. For GEF zeros, strong clustering and variance bounds for smooth linear statistics verify these assumptions. The proof combines a mixed-cumulant estimate with the partition formula for ordinary and factorial cumulants.
item.dc:creator: Xiaolin Zhu, Feng Guo

item.title: A Central Limit Theorem for Intrinsic Fr\'echet Means on Real Grassmannians
item.description: arXiv:2610.24159v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Subspace-valued data arise in dimension reduction, image-set and video recognition, and signal processing, and the Fr\'echet mean is their standard sample mean [12,10,16,24]. We establish a central limit theorem for the intrinsic sample Fr\'echet mean of i.i.d. observations on the real Grassmann manifold $\mathrm{Gr}(p,n)$, as a specialization of the general theorem of [19]. Unlike prior results which require the distribution to vanish or place negligible mass near the cut locus of the population mean, we allow a continuous, possibly positive density. To enable our results, we derive two properties of $\mathrm{Gr}(p,n)$: the first is that the union of the cut loci of all points within distance $\delta$ of the mean has volume $O(\delta)$. The second is that the Hessian of the squared distance function is integrable. We also give a smooth density on $\mathrm{Gr}(1,2)$ for which the mean is unique but the Fr\'echet Hessian vanishes.
item.dc:creator: Bipayan Banerjee, Imon Banerjee, Swagatam Das

item.title: Rapid Mixing for Sampling Colorings of Random Graphs up to Tree Uniqueness Threshold
item.description: arXiv:2610.25391v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the mixing time of the single-site Glauber dynamics for sampling proper $q$-colorings on sparse Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi random graphs $\mathcal{G}(n, d/n)$. We prove that, whenever $q \ge (1 + o_d(1))d$, Glauber dynamics mixes in polynomial time with high probability over $\mathcal{G}(n, d/n)$ for all sufficiently large integers $n$. This improves the previous bound $q = (\alpha^* + o_d(1))d$ where $\alpha^* = 1.7632...$ is the unique solution of $x = \exp(1/x)$ on $[1, \infty)$ by Efthymiou, Hayes, \v{S}tefankovi\v{c}, and Vigoda (SODA, 2018) and asymptotically matches the uniqueness threshold on infinite regular trees. Our proof has three main ingredients. First we establish logarithmic bounds on the spectral and coupling independence constants of the Gibbs distribution by extending the tree analysis of Chen, Liu, Mani, and Moitra (J. ACM, 2026). Second, we extend the entropy-factorization framework for two-spin systems on random graphs, developed by Bez\'akov\'a, Galanis, Goldberg, and \v{S}tefankovi\v{c} (TALG, 2024), to proper colorings by introducing a buffer around high-degree vertices. Finally, we compare the resulting heat-bath block dynamics with the single-site Glauber dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Zhidan Li, Kuan Yang

item.title: Critical measures and coefficient limits for non-Gaussian holomorphic chaos
item.description: arXiv:2610.34371v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study critical holomorphic multiplicative chaos with circular iid inputs of unit variance. Writing \(R=|X_1|\), the radially normalized boundary measures converge in probability to a finite measure with almost surely positive mass exactly when \(\mathbb{E}[R^2\log(2+R)]<\infty\); otherwise they converge to zero. Radial and Fourier--radial approximations have distinct sharp \(L^q\) convergence criteria at each \(0<q<1\); convergence at every such order holds for both families exactly when \(\mathbb{E}e^{sR}<\infty\) for every \(0<s<2\). In the positive-limit class, coefficient vectors multiplied by \((\log n)^{1/4}\) and their analytic windows converge stably to Gaussian mixtures determined by the same critical measure. A uniformly bounded input family gives uncountably many coefficient-limit laws inequivalent under nonzero deterministic complex rescaling. We distinguish these laws using exact weighted tails under \(\mathbb{E}I_0(2R)<\infty\), where \(I_0\) is the modified Bessel function, and negative mass moments. For \(\log\mathbb{P}(R>u)\sim-\lambda u^\alpha\), \(0<\alpha<1\) and \(\lambda>0\), the normalization and Gaussian-mixture form persist, while every positive limit moment diverges; we determine the logarithmic tails. Finite limiting moments need not imply convergence of the original coefficient moments. In the positive-limit class, coefficient periodograms recover the critical measure and energy normalization gives Gaussian limits. Hardy nonmembership holds under finite variance alone; the positive-limit class has sharp weighted Bergman criteria for \(0<p\le2\) and boundary Sobolev threshold \(s=-1/2\).
item.dc:creator: Feng Guo

item.title: Cutoff for random Cayley graphs of finite groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.41347v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the random walk on a Cayley graph of a finite group whose generators are chosen independently and uniformly at random. We show that, for every finite group, the walk exhibits cutoff with high probability whenever the number of generators is at least a constant multiple of the logarithm of the order of the group and small compared with every positive power of it. This holds for both undirected and directed Cayley graphs, in discrete and continuous time, and the lower bound on the number of generators is best possible, up to the value of the constant. The cutoff time is the time at which the expected entropy of the walk comes close to its maximum, and in general it depends on the structure of the group. This settles a conjecture of Aldous and Diaconis.
item.dc:creator: Haoran Zhu

item.title: Nonlinear PDEs with modulated dispersion II: Korteweg-de Vries equation
item.description: arXiv:1406.7675v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: (Due to the limit on the number of characters for an abstract set by arXiv, the full abstract can not be displayed here. See the abstract in the paper.) We study dispersive equations with a time non-homogeneous modulation acting on the linear dispersion term. As primary models, we consider the Korteweg-de Vries equation (KdV) and related equations such as the Benjamin-Ono equation (BO) and the intermediate long wave equation (ILW), imposing certain irregularity conditions on the time non-homogeneous modulation. In this work, we establish phenomena called regularization by noise in three-folds: (i) When the modulation is sufficiently irregular, we show that the modulated KdV on both the circle and the real line is locally well-posed in the regime where the (unmodulated) KdV equation is known to be ill-posed. In particular, given any $s \in \mathbb R$, we show that the modulated KdV on the circle with a sufficiently irregular modulation is locally well-posed in $H^s(\mathbb T)$. Moreover, by adapting the $I$-method to the current modulated setting, we prove global well-posedness of the modulated KdV in negative Sobolev spaces. (ii) It is known that certain (semilinear) dispersive equations such as BO and ILW exhibit quasilinear nature. We show that sufficiently irregular modulations make the modulated versions of these equations semilinear by establishing their local well-posedness by a contraction argument, providing local Lipschitz continuity of the solution map. (iii) We also prove nonlinear smoothing for these modulated equations, where we show that a gain of regularity of the nonlinear part becomes (arbitrarily) larger for more irregular modulations. As applications of our approach, we also include further examples.
item.dc:creator: Khalil Chouk, Massimiliano Gubinelli, Guopeng Li, Jiawei Li, Tadahiro Oh

item.title: $q$-Bernstein functions and applications
item.description: arXiv:1602.02956v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We characterize q-Bernstein functions by exponential tests and, on a geometric lattice, by a well-defined spectral q-Laplace convolution semigroup. We also establish results on q-completely monotonic, q-log-completely monotonic, and q-Bernstein functions and give applications to q-gamma functions.
item.dc:creator: Valmir Krasniqi, Toufik Mansour

item.title: Beating the average: how to generate profit by exploiting the inefficiencies of soccer betting
item.description: arXiv:2303.16648v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In economy, markets are denoted as efficient when it is impossible to systematically generate profits which outperform the average. In the past years, the concept has been tested in other domains such as the growing sports betting market. Surprisingly, despite its large size and its level of maturity, sports betting shows traits of inefficiency. The anomalies indicate the existence of strategies which shift betting from a game of chance towards a game of skill. This article shows an example for an inefficiency detected in the German soccer betting TOTO 13er Wette, which is operated by state-run lottery agencies. Gamblers have to guess the outcome (win, draw, loss) of 13 soccer matches listed on a lottery tip. Applying stochastic methods, a recipe is presented to determine hit rates for single match outcomes. More important, the recipe provides the number of lottery tips required to achieve a specific number of strikes (number of correct match forecasts per lottery tip) for any given level of safety. An approximation is derived to cope with large numbers in hypergeometric distributions, valid under certain constraints. Overall, the strategy does lead to returns exceeding the aggregated lottery fees, resulting in moderate, but consistent profits. It is briefly discussed if lessons learned from soccer betting can be transferred back to financial markets, because gamblers and retail investors face similar challenges and opportunities.
item.dc:creator: Ralph St\"ommer

item.title: Achieving Exponential Asymptotic Optimality in Average-Reward Restless Bandits without Global Attractor Assumption
item.description: arXiv:2405.17882v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider the infinite-horizon average-reward restless bandit problem. We propose a novel two-set policy that maintains two dynamic subsets of arms: one subset of arms has a nearly optimal state distribution and takes actions according to an LP-Priority routine; the other subset of arms is driven towards the optimal state distribution and gradually merged into the first subset. We show that our two-set policy is asymptotically optimal with an $O(\exp(-C N))$ optimality gap for an $N$-armed problem, under the assumptions of aperiodic-unichain, non-degeneracy, and local stability. Our policy is the first to achieve exponential asymptotic optimality under the above set of easy-to-verify assumptions, whereas prior work either requires a global attractor assumption or only achieves an $O(1/\sqrt{N})$ optimality gap. We further discuss obstacles in weakening the assumptions by demonstrating examples where exponential asymptotic optimality is not achievable when any of the three assumptions is violated. Notably, we prove a lower bound for a large class of locally unstable restless bandits, showing that local stability is particularly fundamental for exponential asymptotic optimality. Finally, we use simulations to demonstrate that the two-set policy outperforms previous policies on certain restless bandit problems and performs competitively overall.
item.dc:creator: Yige Hong, Qiaomin Xie, Yudong Chen, Weina Wang

item.title: Private Minimum Hellinger Distance Estimation via Hellinger Distance Differential Privacy
item.description: arXiv:2501.14974v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Objective functions based on Hellinger distance yield robust and efficient estimators of model parameters. Motivated by privacy and regulatory requirements encountered in contemporary applications, we derive in this paper \emph{private minimum Hellinger distance estimators}. The estimators satisfy a new privacy constraint, namely, Hellinger differential privacy, while retaining the robustness and efficiency properties. We demonstrate that Hellinger differential privacy shares several features of standard differential privacy while allowing for sharper inference. Additionally, for computational purposes, we also develop Hellinger differentially private gradient descent and Newton-Raphson algorithms. We illustrate the behavior of our estimators in finite samples using numerical experiments and verify that they retain robustness properties under gross-error contamination.
item.dc:creator: Fengnan Deng, Anand N. Vidyashankar

item.title: Canonical Forms as Dual Volumes
item.description: arXiv:2509.02239v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study dual volume representations of canonical forms for positive geometries in projective spaces, expressing their rational canonical functions as Laplace transforms of measures supported on the convex dual of the semialgebraic set. More generally, for hyperbolic positive geometries the inverse Laplace transform is naturally understood as a distribution supported on the closed dual cone. When this distribution is a non-negative measure, we term the geometry completely monotone, reflecting the property of its canonical function. We identify a class of positive geometries with hyperbolic algebraic boundary for which this cone-supported distribution exists. In particular, simplex-like minimal spectrahedra are completely monotone, with representing measures governed by the Riesz--Wishart theory of the cone of positive semidefinite matrices and admitting integral descriptions over spectrahedral slices and lower-rank strata. We explicitly compute these measures for positive geometries in the projective plane bounded by lines and conics or by a nodal cubic, revealing periods evaluating to transcendental functions. This dual volume perspective replaces logarithmic differential forms by dual measures in the completely monotone case, forging new connections to hyperbolic differential operators, convex optimization and algebraic statistics.
item.dc:creator: Elia Mazzucchelli, Prashanth Raman

item.title: Partition Functions of Two-Dimensional Coulomb Gases with Circular Root- and Jump-Type Singularities
item.description: arXiv:2510.00843v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we study the random polynomial $p_n(\rho):=\prod_{j=1}^n (|z_j|-\rho)$, where the points $\{z_j\}_{j=1}^n$ are the eigenvalues of random normal matrices with a radially symmetric potential. We establish precise large $n$ asymptotic expansions for the moment generating function $\mathbb{E}\bigl[{\rm e}^{(u \operatorname{Im}\log p_n(\rho))/\pi} {\rm e}^{a\operatorname{Re}\log p_n(\rho)}\bigr]$, $u\in\mathbb{R}$, $a>-1$, where $\rho>0$ lies in the bulk of the spectral droplet. The asymptotic expansion is expressed in terms of parabolic cylinder functions, which confirms a conjecture of Byun and Charlier. This also provides the first free energy expansion of two-dimensional Coulomb gases with general circular root- and jump-type singularities. While the $a=0$ case has already been widely studied in the literature due to its relation to counting statistics, we also obtain new results for this special case.
item.dc:creator: Kohei Noda

item.title: Propagation of Chaos in Contextual Flow Maps
item.description: arXiv:2605.16747v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a quantitative statistical theory of transformers in the large-context regime by adopting the abstraction of contextual flow maps (CFMs): dynamical systems that evolve a distinguished token in the presence of a contextual measure across a stack of attention blocks. Within this framework, the finite-context model approximates an idealized infinite-context system in which the contextual measure is replaced by its underlying population, so that the context length $n$ becomes a statistical resource. Exploiting the McKean--Vlasov structure of the dynamics and the classical machinery of propagation of chaos, we establish a forward bound controlling the deviation between the finite- and infinite-context CFMs uniformly along depth, and a backward bound controlling the deviation between the corresponding training trajectories uniformly across iterations of online gradient descent. Both bounds achieve the optimal Wasserstein rate $n^{-1/d}$ for general CFMs and parametric rate $n^{-1/2}$ for a restricted class of CFMs that includes transformers as a special case. The analysis rests on a new Eulerian adjoint formulation of the loss gradient and stability estimates for the resulting forward--adjoint system, both of which may be of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Shi Chen, Zhengjiang Lin, Kaizhao Liu, Philippe Rigollet

item.title: Entropy Bounds for Local Coordination and Graph Amenability
item.description: arXiv:2606.01963v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study local coordination on finite graphs, equivalently, the ability of randomized local protocols with independent private randomness to produce highly correlated outputs at neighboring vertices. Hutchcroft, Rospuskova, and Tamuz (2026) showed that if such local coordination can be achieved with low cost, then the graph admits a low-cost leader profile, or equivalently an appropriate bounded-radius decomposition, with a square-root loss in the cost. We substantially improve this bound for unbiased binary outputs. If the average disagreement is $\varepsilon$, we construct a leader profile of cost $O(\varepsilon\log(1/\varepsilon))$. The key ingredient is an information-theoretic influence measure: after fixing an ordering of the independent information sources, we assign to each binary output the increments of mutual information revealed along that ordering. For two outputs that disagree with probability $p$, the corresponding measures are within binary entropy $h(p)$ in total variation. Combined with a grand coupling theorem, this yields the improved bound. We also show that a universal linear bound is impossible. We construct graphs with binary local profiles of cost $O(\varepsilon)$ for which every leader profile has cost $$ \Omega\!\left(\varepsilon\sqrt{\log(1/\varepsilon)}\right). $$ The construction uses weighted majority functions and can be implemented as an action-symmetric Nash equilibrium, giving a negative answer to the question of HRT whether leader equilibria are always optimal up to a constant factor. Finally, we show that the binary assumption is essential: for general real-valued outputs, the square-root dependence of the HRT theorem is sharp up to a universal constant.
item.dc:creator: Ron Peretz, Dean Kraizberg

item.title: Temporal Conductance and Bounds on the Voter Model for Dynamic Networks
item.description: arXiv:2606.13374v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The voter model is a classical stochastic process that models how opinions might spread through a network: at each step, every node lazily adopts the opinion of a random neighbour; eventually all nodes share the same opinion (consensus). Stronger connectivity should yield faster consensus. Berenbrink, Giakkoupis, Kermarrec, and Mallmann-Trenn (ICALP 2016) make this precise via the network's conductance: if the network has $m$ edges, minimum degree $d_{\min}$, and conductance at least $\phi$, then the voter model reaches consensus in expected $O(m/(d_{\min}\phi))$ steps. Their results extend to dynamic networks with fixed vertex degrees by considering the network's conductance at each time step. We introduce temporal conductance $\Phi$, a more general connectivity measure for dynamic networks. Unlike static conductance, which collapses to $0$ whenever some snapshot is disconnected, $\Phi$ captures connectivity through edges that appear at different times. We generalise the results of Berenbrink et al. from static conductance to temporal conductance, showing that the expected consensus time of the standard voter model is at most $O(m/(d_{\min}\Phi))$. Moreover, we prove that this bound is tight up to constant factors. We expect temporal conductance to be a useful primitive for analysing other dynamics on temporal networks, and potentially time-inhomogeneous Markov chains more generally.
item.dc:creator: Tatiana Rocha Avila, Holger Dell, John Lapinskas

item.title: The five vertex model on a rectangle
item.description: arXiv:2606.22004v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We derive a determinantal expression for the inhomogeneous asymmetric five vertex model in a rectangular geometry with arbitrary boundary conditions at the bottom and top. Standard non-intersecting lattice path, or free fermion, approaches are not applicable and the determinantal form thus is not immediate.
item.dc:creator: Jan de Gier, Richard Kenyon, Michael Wheeler, Yuyang Zhou

item.title: Cost of one-relator groups
item.description: arXiv:2606.23506v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For any infinite one-relator group $\Gamma=\langle S \mid w^m\rangle$, we prove that $\mathrm{cost}(\Gamma)=|S|-\frac{1}{m}$. For such groups, this gives $\beta^{(2)}_1(\Gamma)=\mathrm{cost}(\Gamma) - 1$, answering a special case of Gaboriau's question on the relationship between cost and first $\ell^2$-Betti number.
item.dc:creator: Antoine Poulin, Konrad Wr\'obel

item.title: Mean Field Reinforcement Learning: Theory and Algorithms for Mean Field Control
item.description: arXiv:2607.01525v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This monograph provides an introduction to mean field reinforcement learning through the lens of Markov decision processes arising from large-population stochastic control with mean field interactions and common noise. Starting from the connection between multi-agent reinforcement learning and mean field control, it develops the probabilistic, mathematical, and control-theoretic framework needed to formulate representative-agent learning problems, analyze their relationship with finite-population systems, and study both general and linear-quadratic models. The presentation includes dynamic programming principles, propagation-of-chaos limits, and theoretical analyses of tabular Q-learning and policy-gradient methods. It also discusses numerical implementations, including tabular schemes and deep reinforcement learning methods such as deep deterministic policy gradient. The goal is to give readers a coherent bridge between mean field control theory and reinforcement learning methodology, emphasizing the mathematical structure of the problems and the design of tractable learning approaches for large stochastic populations.
item.dc:creator: Ren\'e Carmona, Mathieu Lauri\`ere

item.title: On the diffusive-mean field limit of a kinetic weakly interacting particle system
item.description: arXiv:2607.15896v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the joint diffusive-mean field limit for a system of weakly interacting kinetic Langevin dynamics, extending the results of Delgadino, Gvalani and Pavliotis (Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal., 2021) to the hypoelliptic/hypocoercive case. We show that, in the absence of phase transitions, the two limits commute, and we calculate the covariance matrix of the limiting Brownian motion using the Green-Kubo/Kipnis-Varadhan formula. However, at low temperatures, and in the presence of phase transitions, the two limits may not commute. We demonstrate our findings by providing a detailed analysis of the diffusive-mean field limit for the $O(2)$ model in a magnetic field. Our analysis is based on the systematic use of recently developed hypocoercivity techniques, together with an appropriate linearization of the mean field McKean-Vlasov-Fokker-Planck partial differential equation.
item.dc:creator: Rapha\"el Gastaldello, Grigorios A. Pavliotis, Gabriel Stoltz, Urbain Vaes

item.title: Random unitary circuits with constant spectral gap
item.description: arXiv:2607.20919v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove constant lower bounds for the spectral gap of the following random walks on unitary groups $\mathsf{SU}(2^n)$ on $n$ qubits. (i) Random Pauli Rotation: choose an $n$-qubit Pauli operator $P$ and an angle $\theta \in [0,2\pi)$, both uniformly at random, and apply $e^{\mathrm i \theta P}$. (ii) Brickwork Random Unitary Circuit: choose $n-1$ unitaries $U_{i}$ uniformly at random from $\mathsf{SU}(4)$ (including central phases of the parent group) independently, and apply $U_{2j-1}$ on two qubits $2j-1, 2j$ and then $U_{2j}$ on two qubits $2j, 2j+1$. Importantly, the gap bounds are independent of $n$ and apply for all finite dimensional unitary representations of $\mathsf{SU}(2^n)$ uniformly. Our results immediately imply that the Random Pauli Rotation and Brickwork Random Unitary Circuit converge to approximate unitary $t$-designs after $\mathcal{O}(nt)$ steps. As a consequence, we improve implications for the complexity growth of random unitary circuits as a function of the depth. The existing argument can be applied almost verbatim, but previously the depth had to be $\mathcal{O}(2^{cn})$ for some $c < 1$. Our unconditional constant spectral gap removes this restriction. We prove analogous constant-gap results for orthogonal and Clifford groups; the latter is indispensable for our result on the Brickwork Random Unitary Circuit. The former implies convergence to approximate orthogonal $t$-designs. In this case, the implied mixing time with respect to a constant additive and multiplicative error is optimal (up to an absolute constant factor) for $t=2$.
item.dc:creator: Tim Baer, Jeongwan Haah

item.title: Dimension-Free Lipschitz Bounds for Brenier Maps to Compact Log-Concave Targets
item.description:
arXiv:2608.15906v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $d\geq1$, $\Lambda>0$, and $ho\in\mathbb{R}$, let $\mu=\mathcal{N}(0,\Lambda^{-1}\mathrm{Id})$ on $\mathbb{R}^{d}$, where $\mathrm{Id}$ is the identity matrix, and let $
u$ be a probability measure whose support is a convex body $K$ of diameter $D=\operatorname{diam}(K)$ and whose density is proportional to $e^{-W}$, where $\mathrm{D}^{2}W\succeq-ho\mathrm{Id}$. We prove that the Brenier map $T$ from $\mu$ to $
u$ has Lipschitz constant $\operatorname{Lip}(T)\leq\sqrt{\Lambda/(2\pi)}\int_{-D/2}^{D/2}e^{ho t^{2}/2}\,\mathrm{d}t$, which is sharp in every fixed dimension. For log-concave targets, the optimal coefficient of $\sqrt{\Lambda}\,D$ is $1/\sqrt{2\pi}$. For sources with finite second moment and density proportional to $e^{-V}$ for which $x\mapsto rac12\langle Qx,xangle-V(x)$ is convex, where $Q$ is symmetric positive definite, and log-concave targets with compact support $K$, the Brenier potential $\Phi$ satisfies $\partial_{vv}\Phi\leq C_{1}\sqrt{\langle Qv,vangle}\,w_{K}(v)$ in the sense of distributions, where $w_{K}(v):=\sup_{y\in K}\langle y,vangle-\inf_{y\in K}\langle y,vangle$ is the width of $K$ along $v\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$ and $C_{1}<0.463$. This removes Kolesnikov's $\sqrt d$ loss. For log-concave sources with $\mathrm{D}^{2}V\preceq\Lambda\mathrm{Id}$ and the target $
u$, the Brenier map $T$ satisfies $\operatorname{Lip}(T)^{2}\leq\Lambda\int_{0}^{D^{2}/4}e^{ho t}\,\mathrm{d}t$, so $\operatorname{Lip}(T)$ has the optimal exponential rate $1/8$ in $ho D^{2}$.
item.dc:creator: Maja Gwozdz

item.title: A Probability Model for Pentagonal Prism Dice Rolls
item.description: arXiv:2609.01643v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In the realm of probability theory and game design, the study of dice probabilities plays a crucial role. The featured dice are usually fair, so their probabilities can be predicted without rolling the dice. Pentagonal prismatic dice are not fair. Hence, the probabilities are more complicated. Our mathematical model is naturally derived from both the geometric properties of the dice and empirical evidence. Dice of varying sizes but with constant volume were designed. Using a 3D printer with 100 percent infill, the dice were printed and prepared. A machine that simulates dropping dice through a dice tower onto a hard surface was used to obtain about 41,000 results. From these data, a statistical model was constructed that gives probabilities of dice with varying height-to-radius ratios. The formula for the model is based on the centroid solid angle, but with two adjustment parameters due to varying energy and other requirements to transition between different resting aspects. Within the range of height-to-radius ratios tested, the data are within reasonable statistical error of the model.
item.dc:creator: Paul R. Hurst, J. Naleo Hyde

item.title: Spatial Mixing and Deterministic Approximate Counting of Multi-spin Systems beyond Bounded Degree Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2609.12352v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a framework for deterministic approximate counting of multi-spin systems beyond bounded-degree graphs. The algorithm recursively constructs rational polytopes containing the true marginal vectors and uses linear-fractional programming to obtain certified bounds on marginal ratios. For positive interactions on graphs of polynomial connective constant $D$, we establish strong spatial mixing whenever $Dc<1$, where $c$ bounds the Birkhoff contraction coefficients of the interactions. Under the same condition, we also give a deterministic fully polynomial-time approximation scheme (\textbf{FPTAS}) for the partition function. We further extend the framework to proper colorings of sparse Erd\H{o}s-R\'{e}nyi random graphs using recursion on permissive blocks. For every fixed $\eta\in(0,1)$, sufficiently large fixed $d$, and fixed integer $q\ge(2+\eta)d$, we obtain an \textbf{FPTAS} for counting proper $q$-colorings of $G\sim\mathcal G(n,d/n)$ with high probability over $G$. This improves the leading constant $3$ in the earlier counting guarantee of Yin and Zhang (APPROX/RANDOM, 2016) to $2$, and asymptotically matches the spatial mixing regime established by Yin (ICALP, 2014).
item.dc:creator: Zhidan Li, Kuan Yang

item.title: Sublinear Markov Semigroups Beyond Uniqueness
item.description: arXiv:2609.37881v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: To what extent does a local operator on smooth test functions determine a sub-Markov semigroup and its underlying structure of laws? Many existing approaches work with Feller semigroups on the space \(C_b\) of bounded continuous functions and rely on uniqueness, often established through a comparison principle for the associated evolution equation. However, even when the local operator is linear, uniqueness may fail and a \(C_b\)-Feller restriction may exclude the associated canonical semigroup. We discover that the space \(\operatorname{USC}_b\) of bounded upper semicontinuous functions offers a natural setting for this study. Within this framework, a complete description of the relationships among sublinear local operators, sublinear sub-Markov semigroups, and their underlying structures of laws is achieved without assuming uniqueness. Under suitable regularity and Lyapunov conditions, we construct the greatest semigroup compatible with a prescribed sublinear local operator and obtain a stochastic representation in terms of a Markov process under sublinear expectations. We characterize all sublinear sub-Markov semigroups dominated by this greatest semigroup in two ways: through a one-to-one correspondence with stable subfamilies of its representing laws, and through an order relation between their infinitesimal generators and the prescribed local operator. We further characterize the greatest semigroup via the greatest viscosity subsolution of the associated Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equation. These results clarify what information about global stochastic evolution can be recovered from local infinitesimal descriptions and what freedom remains in the absence of uniqueness. The resulting characterizations are new even when the local operator is linear.
item.dc:creator: Jongjin Park, David Criens, Hyungbin Park

item.title: A Tale of Two Walks: From Kac to KMP and Back
item.description: arXiv:2609.38044v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We reveal an unexpected connection between two interacting particle systems: Kac's walk and the Kipnis-Marchioro-Presutti (KMP) process. We first establish a mixing-time analogue of Aldous's conjecture for the KMP process on general graphs: the mixing time of the $t$-particle process on any connected $d$-vertex graph is at most $O(\log d)$ times the corresponding single-particle mixing time, uniformly in $t$. As an application, we improve the mixing-time bound for coordinate hit-and-run on the $n$-dimensional standard simplex from $\widetilde{O}(n^3)$ [KV26] to $O(n\log n)$, while removing the dependence on the initial distribution. We then show that the twirling channel induced by the parallel Kac's walk on the symmetric subspace can be exactly encoded by a Markov chain on partitions, which naturally lifts to a parallel KMP chain on the complete graph. We prove that $O(\log d+\log(1/\varepsilon))$ repetitions of the parallel Kac's walk suffice to approximate Haar twirling on the symmetric subspace of $(\mathbb{C}^d)^{\otimes t}$ to error $\varepsilon$, uniformly in all $t$. Our main technical contribution is a new structural property of KMP-type dynamics: conditional product structure, which holds for both the standard KMP processes on general graphs and the parallel KMP processes on complete graphs. Conditioned on suitable auxiliary randomness, the evolution of the labeled KMP process factorizes into independent single-particle updates. Combining this structure with an exact coupling inspired by the analysis of Kac's walk, we remove the dependence on the number of particles from the mixing bounds for both unlabeled KMP models. This bypasses the $\log(\pi_{\min}^{-1})$ dependency from spectral-gap arguments, which is often prohibitively large for many-particle systems. Using this framework, we prove mixing bounds that are sharp up to logarithmic factors for both unlabeled KMP models.
item.dc:creator: Qian Chen, Jingcheng Liu, Minglong Qin, Leonard J. Schulman, Fang Song, Penghui Yao, Mingnan Zhao

item.title: Beyond light cones: State preparation complexity in quantum spin glasses
item.description: arXiv:2610.02166v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a technique for studying state preparation complexity in the quantum $p$-spin model on $n$ qubits, a disordered quantum spin system with random interactions on every set of $p$ qubits. We reduce the task of proving state preparation lower bounds to bounding the local profile complexity of the class, a quantity derived from the metric entropy of the set of vectors recording each state's expectation values against all weight-$p$ Pauli strings. We show that, for sufficiently large fixed $p$, any class with local profile complexity $O(n^2)$ remains separated from the ground-state energy by $\Omega(\sqrt n)$, a gap on the leading energy scale. When the profile complexity is $o(n^2)$, we prove the stronger conclusion that the class cannot outperform a benchmark class of simpler states at leading order. Product states always provide such a benchmark. Our framework strengthens known bounds and covers classes beyond the reach of previous methods. These include examples where circuit lightcones extend across the entire system, preventing an application of standard arguments. We obtain an $\Omega(n^2/\log n)$ gate lower bound for preparing near-ground states and depth--width tradeoffs, allowing arbitrary one- and two-qubit gates and arbitrarily many discardable ancillas. We also derive lower bounds on entanglement depth and matrix product state bond dimension, and energy obstructions for forward and reverse magic at every fixed level of Parham's magic hierarchy (arXiv:2504.19966). For Clifford circuits doped with $T$-gates, we obtain sharper energy comparisons using product stabilizer states as a more restrictive benchmark. The proof combines an adaptation of a nonsymmetric quantum de Finetti theorem (arXiv:1810.12197) with metric-entropy bounds for the Gaussian process indexed by the local profiles of states in the class.
item.dc:creator: Omar Al-Ghattas, David Gamarnik, Bobak T Kiani

item.title: Measuring the roughness of a signal
item.description: arXiv:2610.05457v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the non-parametric estimation of the roughness of a path from discretely sampled observations. Our approach is based on the concept of normalized power variation of a path. The estimator identifies a variation index by comparing coarse increments with local sums of fine increments. We prove pathwise consistency under H\"older regularity, nondegenerate coarse critical power sums, uniform local bounds on fine critical power sums, and separation of the two sampling scales and obtain a convergence rate for the estimator. Neither convergence of critical variation nor monotonicity of the finite-sample statistic is required. The result applies to fractional Brownian motion under dyadic sampling and to Schauder series with bounded coefficients bounded away from zero. For signed Takagi--Landsberg functions we obtain a uniform asymptotic formula and a quantitative bound for every root of the estimating equation in a fixed parameter interval. For fractional Brownian motion, we obtain asymptotic uniqueness of the estimating root and a polynomial almost-sure error bound. We illustrate the results with numerical experiments for Takagi-Landsberg functions, fractional Brownian motion and the stochastic heat equation.
item.dc:creator: Rama Cont, Purba Das

item.title: Positive Bidiagonal Factorizations and Mixed-Type Chebyshev Multiple Orthogonal Polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.08568v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We characterize when a semi-infinite banded totally positive matrix admits a positive bidiagonal factorization, without assuming boundedness, and establish criteria for stability under perturbations. These criteria distinguish whether the initial factor entries are fixed or allowed to vary. For banded totally positive Toeplitz matrices, such factorizations always exist; a factorization can be chosen to depend analytically on all sufficiently small perturbations within the same band if and only if the polynomial symbol has distinct roots. Explicit root formulas determine the associated mixed-type multiple orthogonal polynomials and their matrix of positive measures. They also yield scalar linear forms independent of the chosen factorization, from which we obtain asymptotic zero spacing and sine-kernel limits. We further treat finite boundary modifications and limiting zero distributions for matrices with convergent diagonals.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Ma\~nas

item.title: Fast Almost-Uniform Sampling of Random $k$-SAT Solutions
item.description: arXiv:2610.10474v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study approximately uniform sampling of satisfying assignments from random $k$-SAT formulas. Fix a constant $B>0$. For every $k\ge 2^{20}$ and density $0<\alpha\le 2^k/k^{16}$, we prove that, with high probability over a random formula on $n$ variables, every accuracy $n^{-B}\le\varepsilon\le 1/2$ admits a sampler whose output distribution is within total variation distance $\varepsilon$ of the uniform distribution on satisfying assignments with expected running time $$\widetilde O_B\left(\mathrm{poly}(k,\alpha+1)n^{2+\eta}\right),\quad 0<\eta\le 2^{16-k}.$$ In particular, the exponent of $n$ is $2+O(2^{-k})$ while the dependence on the width and density is polynomial with a universal degree. This improves the parameter-dependent polynomial exponent of the sampling algorithm of Chen, Lonkar, Wang, Yang, and Yin (STOC 2025) in the density regime $2^k/\mathrm{poly}(k)$. Our algorithm separates a high-degree core from the remaining variables. Every residual formula on the good variables is a deletion subformula of a common bounded-dependency formula. Adapting the rejection--repair framework of Liu, Wang, Yin, Zhang and Zhou (arXiv 2026), we construct an executable sampler for all such residual formulas using ordinary connected violation sets replacing weighted 2-tree witnesses and use it to simulate approximate block heat-bath updates on the core. To analyze the resulting core chain, we integrate out the good variables, represent the core marginal by an absolutely convergent polymer expansion and combine a component-swap variance comparison with an adaptive exploration bound. Absorbing single-component interactions into the local weights leaves interactions of cluster size at least two; retaining their additional decay gives a spectral gap of at least $1/(2s n^{2^{12-k}})$ where $s$ counts core components. Together with the residual sampler, this yields the stated running time.
item.dc:creator: Kun He, Zhidan Li, Kuan Yang

item.title: Measure Theory in Convergence Spaces Part II: Abstract Integration in Net Convergence Structures
item.description: arXiv:2610.21014v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The construction of a coherent and general integration procedure is the central question of this second part of our study of measure theory in convergence spaces. We define, and establish convergence theorems for such process of integration, called the net Riemann integration, in convergence groups and commutative monoids, preserving the prescribed convergence throughout. The underlying interchange theorem admits noncommutative groups and requires right completeness only at the cardinality of the error family. Under intrinsic stability assumptions, countable error control therefore needs only sequential completeness, even for arbitrary integration nets, from which we also stablish a general version of Henstock's lemma. The resulting uniform theorems reaches incomplete ranges in which no complete subspace contains a tail of the approximating integrals. In the ordered locally solid convergence theory side, countability of the inner direction replaces countable accessibility of the approximants, and local existence arguments yield monotone and dominated convergence and, under additional controller assumptions, a further extension through increasing integrable barriers with pointwise coverage and uniformly vanishing excess primitives. This constructs the limiting integral without a common integrable envelope and gives uniform control of primitive variation. We finish with two appendices on new and general results of abstract metrization of net convergences and related topics.
item.dc:creator: Alexandre Reggiolli Teixeira

item.title: The semiring of spectral duality skeletons: cancellation, characters and factorization
item.description: arXiv:2610.23684v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Weighted dual skeletons are the combinatorial core of spectral duality structures. Their isomorphism classes, under Cartesian product and disjoint union, form a semiring graded by the degree. We identify it completely: a class is determined by its degree, a symmetric element of the group semiring N_0[R] and its number of fixed points. Equivalently, skeletons of a given degree are finite C_2-sets over the C_2-monoid (R,+), these data are their marks, and the semiring is an infinite-monoid analogue of a crossed Burnside semiring. The multiplicative monoid is not cancellative, the only obstruction being that multiplication by a skeleton without fixed points forgets the fixed points; accordingly, the Grothendieck ring has explicit zero divisors. A continuous family of semiring characters, with the degree and the number of fixed points, is a complete invariant, and for commensurable ratios the multiplicative Grothendieck group is described by P\'olya's theorem. The main subject is factorization. The reduced monoid is atomic with bounded lengths, but factorization is not unique, the elasticity is infinite, and even the divisor-closed submonoid with one fixed point is not half-factorial. Without fixed points, every reducible skeleton splits off a single orbit, which gives a criterion by centers, exactly when the number of orbits is 8, 16, a prime or twice a prime. Irreducibility is generic in almost every type. Progression skeletons factor according to mixed-radix number systems, with all factorizations of equal length. Finally, orbit counting gives the dimension of the separatrix and the response rank of products.
item.dc:creator: Juan Antonio Vega Coso

item.title: A direct obstacle proof of a dimension-free weak-type $(1,1)$ bound for the Gaussian Riesz transforms
item.description: arXiv:2610.26478v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give a detailed, direct proof of a dimension-free weak-type $(1,1)$ estimate for the first-order Gaussian vector Riesz transform, using the fractional obstacle method of Ouyang, Spector, and Stockdale. For $d\gamma_n=\pi^{-n/2}e^{-|x|^2}\,dx$, let $L=-\tfrac12\Delta+x\cdot\nabla$, $D=2^{-1/2}\nabla$, and $R_\gamma=DL^{-1/2}\Pi_0$, where $\Pi_0$ removes the mean. We prove that $R_\gamma$ has weak-type constant at most $2$ on real-valued inputs, independently of $n$. The main construction is the unique unshifted decomposition $F=g+L^{1/2}u$, for nonnegative $F\in L^2(\gamma_n)$ and $a>\int F\,d\gamma_n$, with $u\geq0$, $\min\{F,a\}\leq g\leq a$, preservation of mass, and $g=a$ on $\{u>0\}$. We retain the details of coercivity, the Lewy--Stampacchia estimate, the upgrade from the form domain to the operator domain, and locality. We also identify the $L^1$ extension with the principal-value transform and obtain the constant $8/\pi$ for complex-valued inputs.
item.dc:creator: Cristian E. Guti\'errez, Juan Manfredi

item.title: Statistics of entries of matrices from the general linear group over a finite field
item.description: arXiv:2610.29305v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$ be the group of $n\times n$ invertible matrices over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$. How many matrices in $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$ are there with a subset of their entries prescribed? Motivated by the random matrix theory of classical compact groups, we address this question and various variants, with a focus on asymptotic results that are valid as $n$ tends to infinity. Our methods are Fourier-analytic, with the main input being an exponential sum over $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$, evaluated in 1955 by Hodges via elementary methods. Our results turn out to be related to investigations carried out in other fields, including coding theory, universality for $p$-adic matrices and algebraic combinatorics.
item.dc:creator: Ofir Gorodetsky

item.title: Beyond Brown's radial tests: admissibility, parabolicity, and a doubling-Poincar\'e prior that neither test decides
item.description: arXiv:2610.34309v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For the estimation of a normal mean in $\mathbb{R}^m$ under quadratic loss, Brown (1971) proved that a generalized Bayes estimator $\delta_F$ with bounded drift is admissible if and only if a diffusion attached to the marginal $f^*$ of the prior $F$ is recurrent, and gave two radial tests: a sphere-average test for recurrence and a ray test for transience. He observed that both tests can be silent. We read his theory as the potential theory of the weighted Euclidean space $(\mathbb{R}^m,f^*\,dx)$ and ask what the modern theory of recurrence on weighted manifolds adds inside the zone where neither test applies. Three results. (A) If $f^*\,dx$ is doubling and supports a scale-invariant Poincar\'e inequality, the sphere test is already complete: recurrence, Brown's sphere test and the ball-volume test are equivalent, so geometric criteria can add decidable cases only on the inadmissible side. (B) They do add one. An explicit prior on $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose marginal is small along a lattice of circles at dyadic scales with spacing equal to the square root of the scale, is doubling and Poincar\'e, silences both of Brown's tests, and is transient by the ball-volume test; its generalized Bayes estimator is inadmissible. (C) Outside the doubling-Poincar\'e class the zone is two-sided: the same circles placed on one surface per scale give an admissible estimator, decided by a flux bound along a non-spherical exhaustion, and a logarithmic product prior gives an inadmissible one, decided by product heat kernels. A comparison lemma shows that any positive weight with Lipschitz logarithm is, up to constants, the marginal of a prior, so that explicit weights may be used throughout.
item.dc:creator: Oleg Roshka

item.title: Para-Gaussian Approximations of Random Deep Neural Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.37388v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: It is known that randomly initialized neural networks have Gaussian behaviour in the $n\to \infty$ limit. Unfortunately, this approximation can be poor for finite $n$ and gets worse as one goes deeper into the network. In this work, we develop a more accurate approximation that is \emph{slightly} non-Gaussian, which we call the para-Gaussian distribution and is constructed from the Hermite polynomials. We show how this para-Gaussian approximation can lead to a practical recursive method to approximate the deeper layers of the network. Finally, we apply this theory to linear neural networks (where things can be solved exactly) and to ReLU neural networks (where things can be approximated).
item.dc:creator: Mihai Nica, Janosch Ortmann
